data.title: AI winter is well on its way (2018)
data.author: darkhorse13
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了深度学习在人工智能（AI）革命中的地位变化。尽管几年前深度学习被视为通向技术奇点（通用AI）的捷径，但到2018年中，这种叙事开始出现裂缝，特别是在自动驾驶等实际应用中。尽管表面上的热度仍在，如NIPS会议和企业宣传依旧强调AI，但一些迹象显示出兴趣的减弱。例如，著名研究者的推文活跃度下降，他们的言论受到更多审视。深度学习曾被认为可以轻松扩展，但研究显示，尽管模型计算资源增加千倍，性能提升却有限。例如，视觉模型的性能在AlexNet之后很快达到饱和，而像AlphaGo Zero这样的项目虽然计算量巨大，但实际应用有限。文章暗示，大公司对深度学习的兴趣可能正在减弱，研究者们则转向政府资助机构以确保研究资金。

主要讨论点：对某一阵营或观点的批评策略的分析

不同观点：
• [批评者的立场] ctoth认为，某些评论者采用了一套固定的批评模式，具体表现为：选择性地挑出一些令人失望的地方，将任何策略转变视为退缩，宣称 hype（热潮）不可持续，并预测即将到来的崩溃，进而将自己定位为冷静的现实主义者。这种模式每6-12个月重复一次，并且会在之前的预测没有实现时调整时间线。

• [被批评者的立场] 另一方（即被批评的人或群体）可能认为自己是在进行客观分析，指出潜在问题和风险，并根据事实做出合理的预测。他们可能认为自己的观点并非出于偏见或固定的套路，而是基于对形势的理性判断。

补充讨论：
• ctoth提到的时间线调整（“调整时间线当之前的预测没有实现”）表明这种批评模式有自我延续的特性，即使之前的预测失败，批评者也会通过延长预测的时间范围来维持自己的立场。
• 争议的焦点在于这种批评模式是否真正客观，还是仅仅是一种带有偏见的循环论证。批评者（ctoth）显然认为这是一种不公正的、 cherry-pick（挑刺）式的分析手法，而被批评的一方可能则认为自己在做必要的警示和理性预测。

44474573.article_content:
Deep learning has been at the forefront of the so called AI revolution for quite a few years now, and many people had believed that it is the silver bullet that will take us to the world of wonders of technological singularity (general AI). Many bets were made in 2014, 2015 and 2016 when still new boundaries were pushed, such as the Alpha Go etc.  Companies such as Tesla were announcing through the mouths of their CEO's that fully self driving car was very close, to the point that Tesla even started selling that option to customers [to be enabled by future software update].
We have now mid 2018 and things have changed. Not on the surface yet, NIPS conference is still oversold, the corporate PR still has AI all over its press releases, Elon Musk still keeps promising self driving cars and Google CEO keeps repeating Andrew Ng's slogan that AI is bigger than electricity. But this narrative begins to crack. And
as I predicted in my older post
, the place where the cracks are most visible is autonomous driving - an actual application of the technology in the real world.
The dust settled on deep learning
When the ImageNet was effectively solved (note
this does not mean that vision is solved
), many prominent researchers in the field (including even typically quiet Geoff Hinton) were actively giving press interviews, publicizing stuff on social media (e.g. Yann Lecun, Andrew Ng, Fei-Fei Li to name a few). The general tone was that we are in front of a gigantic revolution and from now on things can only accelerate. Well years have passed and the twitter feeds of those people became less active, as exemplified by Andrew Ng below:
2013 - 0.413 tweets per day
2014 - 0.605 tweets per day
2015 - 0.320 tweets per day
2016 - 0.802 tweets per day
2017 - 0.668 tweets per day
2018 - 0.263 tweets per day (until 24 May)
Perhaps this is because Andrew's outrageous claims are now put to more scrutiny by the community as indicated in a
tweet
below:
Visibly the sentiment has quite considerably declined, there are much fewer tweets praising deep learning as the ultimate algorithm, the papers are becoming less "revolutionary" and much more "evolutionary". Deepmind hasn't shown anything breathtaking since their Alpha Go zero [and even that wasn't that exciting, given the obscene amount of compute necessary and applicability to games only - see
Moravec's paradox
]. OpenAI was rather quiet, with their last media outburst being the
Dota 2 playing agent
[which I suppose was meant to create as much buzz as Alpha Go, but fizzled out rather quickly]. In fact
articles began showing up that even Google in fact does not know what to do with Deepmind
, as their results are apparently not as practical as originally expected... As for the prominent researchers, they've been generally touring around meeting with government officials in Canada or France to secure their future grants, Yann Lecun even
stepped down
(rather symbolically) from the Head of Research to Chief AI scientist at Facebook. This gradual shift from rich, big corporations to government sponsored institutes suggests to me that the interest in this kind of research within these corporations (I think of Google and Facebook) is actually slowly winding down. Again these are all early signs, nothing spoken out loud, just the body language.
Deep learning (does not) scale
One of the key slogans repeated about deep learning is that it scales almost effortlessly. We had the AlexNet in 2012 which had ~60M parameters, we probably now have models with at least 1000x that number right? Well probably we do, the question however is - are these things 1000x as capable? Or even 100x as capable? A study by openAI comes in handy:
So in terms of applications for vision we see that VGG and Resnets saturated somewhat around one order of magnitude of compute resources applied (in terms of number of parameters it is actually less). Xception is a variation of google inception architecture and actually only slightly outperforms inception on ImageNet, arguably actually slightly outperforms everyone else, because essentially AlexNet solved ImageNet. So at 100 times more compute than AlexNet we pretty much saturated architectures in terms of vision, or image classification to be precise. Neural machine translation is a big effort by all the big web search players and no wonder it takes all the compute it can take (and yet google translate still sucks, though has gotten arguably better). The latest three points on that graph, interestingly show reinforcement learning related projects, applied to games by Deepmind and OpenAI. Particularly AlphaGo Zero and slightly more general AlphaZero take ridiculous amount of compute, but are not applicable in the real world applications because much of that compute is needed to simulate and generate the data these data hungry models need. OK, so we can now train AlexNet in minutes rather than days, but can we train a 1000x bigger AlexNet in days and get qualitatively better
44474573.article_summary: 本文讨论了深度学习在人工智能（AI）革命中的地位变化。尽管几年前深度学习被视为通向技术奇点（通用AI）的捷径，但到2018年中，这种叙事开始出现裂缝，特别是在自动驾驶等实际应用中。尽管表面上的热度仍在，如NIPS会议和企业宣传依旧强调AI，但一些迹象显示出兴趣的减弱。例如，著名研究者的推文活跃度下降，他们的言论受到更多审视。深度学习曾被认为可以轻松扩展，但研究显示，尽管模型计算资源增加千倍，性能提升却有限。例如，视觉模型的性能在AlexNet之后很快达到饱和，而像AlphaGo Zero这样的项目虽然计算量巨大，但实际应用有限。文章暗示，大公司对深度学习的兴趣可能正在减弱，研究者们则转向政府资助机构以确保研究资金。

data.title: The Novelty of the Arpanet
data.author: xk3
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了ARPANET的真正创新之处，指出许多人误以为其最大成就是通过网络跨地域连接计算机。然而，ARPANET的突破性不在于简单的远距离连接，而在于它首次展示了计算机网络的社会和经济潜力。1972年10月，在华盛顿希尔顿酒店举行的国际计算机通信会议（ICCC）上，ARPANET首次公开演示。约800名与会者包括计算机科学家及其他领域专业人士，演示通过40个终端和终端接口消息处理器（TIP）展示了网络功能，旨在证明新技术不仅可行而且有用。这一事件标志着计算机网络从技术实验向实际应用的转变。

44428746.article_content:
The Real Novelty of the ARPANET
Networking
07 Feb 2021
If you run an image search for the word “ARPANET,” you will find lots of maps
showing how the
government research
network
expanded steadily across the
country throughout the late ’60s and early ’70s. I’m guessing that most people
reading or hearing about the ARPANET for the first time encounter one of these
maps.
Obviously, the maps are interesting—it’s hard to believe that there were once
so few networked computers that their locations could all be conveyed with what
is really pretty lo-fi cartography. (We’re talking 1960s overhead projector
diagrams here. You know the vibe.) But the problem with the maps, drawn as they
are with bold lines stretching across the continent, is that they reinforce the
idea that the ARPANET’s paramount achievement was connecting computers across
the vast distances of the United States for the first time.
Today, the internet is a lifeline that keeps us tethered to each other even as
an airborne virus has us all locked up indoors. So it’s easy to imagine that,
if the ARPANET was the first draft of the internet, then surely the world that
existed before it was entirely disconnected, since that’s where we’d be without
the internet today, right? The ARPANET must have been a big deal because it
connected people via computers when that hadn’t before been possible.
That view doesn’t get the history quite right. It also undersells what made the
ARPANET such a breakthrough.
The Debut
The Washington Hilton stands near the top of a small rise about a mile and a
half northeast of the National Mall. Its two white-painted modern facades sweep
out in broad semicircles like the wings of a bird. The New York Times,
reporting on the hotel’s completion in 1965, remarked that the building looks
“like a sea gull perched on a hilltop nest.”
1
The hotel hides its most famous feature below ground. Underneath the driveway
roundabout is an enormous ovoid event space known as the International
Ballroom, which was for many years the largest pillar-less ballroom in DC. In
1967, the Doors played a concert there. In 1968, Jimi Hendrix also played a
concert there. In 1972, a somewhat more sedate act took over the ballroom to
put on the inaugural International Conference on Computing Communication, where
a promising research project known as the ARPANET was demonstrated publicly for
the first time.
The 1972 ICCC, which took place from October 24th to 26th, was attended by
about 800 people.
2
It brought together all of the leading researchers in the
nascent field of computer networking. According to internet pioneer Bob Kahn,
“if somebody had dropped a bomb on the Washington Hilton, it would have
destroyed almost all of the networking community in the US at that point.”
3
Not all of the attendees were computer scientists, however. An advertisement
for the conference claimed it would be “user-focused” and geared toward
“lawyers, medical men, economists, and government men as well as engineers and
communicators.”
4
Some of the conference’s sessions were highly technical,
such as the session titled “Data Network Design Problems I” and its sequel
session, “Data Network Design Problems II.” But most of the sessions were, as
promised, focused on the potential social and economic impacts of computer
networking. One session, eerily prescient today, sought to foster a discussion
about how the legal system could act proactively “to safeguard the right of
privacy in the computer data bank.”
5
The ARPANET demonstration was intended as a side attraction of sorts for the
attendees. Between sessions, which were held either in the International
Ballroom or elsewhere on the lower level of the hotel, attendees were free to
wander into the Georgetown Ballroom (a smaller ballroom/conference room down
the hall from the big one),
6
where there were 40 terminals from a variety of
manufacturers set up to access the ARPANET.
7
These terminals were dumb
terminals—they only handled input and output and could do no computation on
their own. (In fact, in 1972, it’s likely that all of these terminals were
hardcopy terminals, i.e. teletype machines.) The terminals were all hooked up
to a computer known as a Terminal Interface Message Processor or TIP, which sat
on a raised platform in the middle of the room. The TIP was a kind of archaic
router specially designed to connect dumb terminals to the ARPANET. Using the
terminals and the TIP, the ICCC attendees could experiment with logging on and
accessing some of the computers at the 29 host sites then comprising the
ARPANET.
8
To exhibit the network’s capabilities, researchers at the host sites across
the country had collaborated to prepare 19 simple “scenarios” for users to
experiment with. These scenarios were compiled into
a
booklet
that was handed to conference attendees as they tentatively approached the maze
of wiring and terminals.
9
The scenarios were meant to prove that the
new technology worked but also that it was useful, because

data.title: Zig breaking change – Initial Writergate
data.author: Retro_Dev
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Zig编程语言中对std.io的重大更改，主要包括废弃现有的std.io读者和写者，引入新的非泛型std.io.Reader和std.io.Writer，并将缓冲区置于接口而非实现中。这些变化虽然具有破坏性，但优化路径依然透明。主要更改包括格式化打印的调整，以及多个函数和方法的重命名与弃用。新API提供了更便捷、性能更好的非泛型接口，并引入了一些独特的流处理概念，如数据丢弃和数据填充。文件读取器还缓存了文件句柄的关键信息，如大小、当前寻址位置和错误信息等。用户需根据新的API调整代码，并使用adaptToNewApi()函数适配旧的流接口。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Zig语言的 breaking changes 及其影响

不同观点：
• **dnautics**：认为Zig的breaking changes并没有造成太大困扰，尤其是对于日常使用者而言。通过维护自己的解析器和扫描整个Zig代码库，可以有效应对变化。同时，作者提到大部分抱怨来自非日常使用者。此外，提到新手面临的挑战，主要是网上过时的示例代码和LLM（大型语言模型）的知识停滞。

• **thrwyexecbrain**：讨论了Zig API的设计，特别是`Reader.stream(writer, limit)`和`Reader.streamRemaining(writer)`函数，认为这些设计在构建数据转换管道时非常优雅。同时也提到`Writer.sendFile()`的独特性，其他语言通常需要直接操作文件描述符。

• **mtlynch**：作为一名Zig开发 hobbyist，对breaking changes感到遗憾，但理解这是使用未到1.0版本语言的一部分。希望Zig团队在帮助迁移方面投入更多，过去的经历显示迁移指导不够明确，尤其是0.12.0版本的构建系统变化。

• **barelysapient**：对重大变化持乐观态度，希望Zig未来能重新审视并改进其他设计选择。

• **samgranieri**：认为如果有良好的linting工具来通知和自动修正，breaking changes并不是大问题。

• **ww520**：提到旧的reader/writer模式在结构体中存储不方便，询问新变化是否解决了这个问题。

• **drtgh**：希望Zig实现某个特定的功能（链接至GitHub issue #5973）。

• **Aissen**：建议开发类似Go的`go fix`工具，用于自动进行语义更改和迁移，认为这对Zig也有帮助。

• **GolDDranks**：虽然写Zig不多，但因为breaking changes对开始严肃项目感到犹豫，同时享受Rust的稳定性。

Previous Scandal
Summary
Deprecates all existing std.io readers and writers in favor of the newly provided
std.io.Reader
and
std.io.Writer
which are
non-generic
and have the buffer above the vtable - in other words the buffer is
in the interface, not the implementation
. This means that although Reader and Writer are no longer generic, they are still transparent to optimization; all of the interface functions have a concrete hot path operating on the buffer, and only make vtable calls when the buffer is full.
I have a lot more changes to upstream but it was taking too long to finish them so I decided to do it more piecemeal. Therefore, I opened this tiny baby PR to get things started.
These changes are extremely breaking. I am sorry for that, but I have carefully examined the situation and acquired confidence that this is the direction that Zig needs to go. I hope you will strap in your seatbelt and come along for the ride; it will be worth it.
The breakage in this first PR mainly has to do with formatted printing.
Upgrade Guide
Turn on
-freference-trace
to help you find all the format string breakage.
std.fs.File.reader -> std.fs.File.deprecatedReader
std.fs.File.writer -> std.fs.File.deprecatedWriter

std.fmt.fmtSliceEscapeLower -> std.ascii.hexEscape
std.fmt.fmtSliceEscapeUpper -> std.ascii.hexEscape
std.fmt.fmtSliceHexLower -> {x}
std.fmt.fmtSliceHexUpper -> {X}
std.fmt.fmtIntSizeDec -> {B}
std.fmt.fmtIntSizeBin -> {Bi}
std.fmt.fmtDuration -> {D}
std.fmt.fmtDurationSigned -> {D}
{} -> {f} when there is a format method. This prevents footguns when adding or deleting format methods.
format method signature
anytype -> *std.io.Writer
inferred error set -> error{WriteFailed}
FormatOptions -> (deleted)
std.fmt.Formatter
now takes context type explicitly
no fmt string
These are deprecated but not deleted yet:
std.io.GenericReader -> std.io.Reader
std.io.GenericWriter -> std.io.Writer
std.io.AnyReader -> std.io.Reader
std.io.AnyWriter -> std.io.Writer
If you have an old stream and you need a new one, you can use
adaptToNewApi()
like this:
fn
foo
(
old_writer
:
anytype

void

var
adapter
=

adaptToNewApi
();
const
w
=
&

.
new_interface
;
try
w
.
print
(
"{s}"
, .{
"example"
});
// ...
}
New API
Formatted Printing
{t} is shorthand for
@tagName()
and
@errorName()
{b64}: output string as standard base64
std.io.Writer
and
std.io.Reader
These have a bunch of handy new APIs that are more convenient, perform better, and are not generic. For instance look at how reading until a delimiter works now.
These streams also feature some unique concepts compared with other languages' stream implementations:
The concept of
discarding
when reading: allows efficiently ignoring data. For instance a decompression stream, when asked to discard a large amount of data, can skip decompression of entire frames.
The concept of
splatting
when writing: this allows a logical "memset" operation to pass through I/O pipelines without actually doing any memory copying, turning an O(M*N) operation into O(M) operation, where M is the number of streams in the pipeline and N is the number of repeated bytes. In some cases it can be even more efficient, such as when splatting a zero value that ends up being written to a file; this can be lowered as a seek forward.
Sending a file when writing: this allows an I/O pipeline to do direct fd-to-fd copying when the operating system supports it.
The stream user provides the buffer, but the stream implementation decides the minimum buffer size. This effectively moves state from the stream implementation into the user's buffer
std.fs.File.Reader
Memoizes key information about a file handle such as:
The size from calling stat, or the error that occurred therein.
The current seek position.
The error that occurred when trying to seek.
Whether reading should be done positionally or streaming.
Whether reading should be done via fd-to-fd syscalls (e.g.
sendfile
)
versus plain variants (e.g.
read
).
Fulfills the
std.io.Reader
interface.

44461067.article_summary: 本文介绍了Zig编程语言中对std.io的重大更改，主要包括废弃现有的std.io读者和写者，引入新的非泛型std.io.Reader和std.io.Writer，并将缓冲区置于接口而非实现中。这些变化虽然具有破坏性，但优化路径依然透明。主要更改包括格式化打印的调整，以及多个函数和方法的重命名与弃用。新API提供了更便捷、性能更好的非泛型接口，并引入了一些独特的流处理概念，如数据丢弃和数据填充。文件读取器还缓存了文件句柄的关键信息，如大小、当前寻址位置和错误信息等。用户需根据新的API调整代码，并使用adaptToNewApi()函数适配旧的流接口。

data.title: Optimizing Tool Selection for LLM Workflows with Differentiable Programming
data.author: viksit
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过本地可学习路由器减少token开销并降低成本的方法，及其在复杂工作流中的应用

不同观点：
• [viksit] 认为可以通过基于PyTorch的学习器和DSPy管道集成来委托工具调用，从而降低成本和token开销。他邀请反馈，并提供了代码示例。
• [pcwelder] 指出，这种方法类似于训练自己的语言模型（LM），而不是使用预训练的大型LM。他认为在某些不需要复杂推理的任务中可以使用较小且更便宜的LM，但这些LM在边缘情况下精度较低。此外，他质疑使用Gumble softmax的必要性，认为常规softmax可能就足够了。
• [crazylogger] 认为在简单的{user_query -> search -> llm_answer}场景中，这种方法是合理的，但在复杂的实际代理流中，工具使用往往是LLM唯一的工作。省略任何一个工具调用记录都会导致代理无法正常工作。
• [Garlef] 质疑选择工具是否是真正的问题，认为更难的是基于上下文确定工具的有效载荷。他建议根据业务需求评估这种方法的价值，而不是一开始就采用。
• [jaksa] 认为选择工具是简单的，传递正确的参数是困难且容易出错的部分。更聪明的代理会根据需要调整工具调用的数量直到获得期望的响应。
• [bGl2YW5j] 认为问题不在于优化LLM的工具选择，而在于让LLM做工具选择本身。他建议使用硬编码规则和分离关注点来处理控制流，认为LLM在处理确定性方面还不够好。

补充讨论：
• [digitcatphd] 认为NVIDIA关于微调小型语言模型的论文提出了一种更有效的方法，暗示可能有更好的技术选择。
• [nphard85] 询问这种方法在复杂的代理工作流中（如使用MCP时）如何工作，还是仅适用于简单情况。
• [shusaku] 认为在使用LLM做所有决策时容易懒惰，但退一步思考是否有更便宜的方法（如硬编码逻辑）是有益的。
• [apsears] 强调LLM有直觉，但他有数据，认为在无法微调LLM时这一点尤为重要。
• [tomlue] 提出可以将损失传播到工具本身，暗示一种可能的技术改进方向。

争议焦点：
• 使用LLM进行工具选择和调用是否是最佳方案，尤其是在复杂工作流中。
• 使用较小且更便宜的LM在实际应用中的可行性及其精度问题。
• 是否应通过硬编码规则和分离关注点来处理控制流，而非依赖LLM。

data.title: Techno-Feudalism and the Rise of AGI: A Future Without Economic Rights?
data.author: lexandstuff
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了人工通用智能（AGI）崛起对经济和政治秩序的冲击。AGI作为既是劳动者又是所有者的角色，正在打破劳动与资本的传统界限，导致经济权力集中于控制其基础设施的少数人手中。这种转变可能加剧不平等，削弱民主机制，并巩固技术封建主义。为避免这种情况，必须重新谈判社会契约，建立新的经济框架，例如通过普遍AI红利、累进税制和去中心化治理，确保AGI带来的繁荣能够公平分配。干预的时机就是现在，以防止智能本身成为最排他的资本形式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AGI（人工智能通用智能）对社会、经济、民主和未来的潜在影响及相关争议

不同观点：
• jandrewrogers认为，AGI可能使大多数人无意识地成为被操控的工具（sock puppets），削弱民主政策反映人民真实意愿的能力。他质疑在AGI广泛应用的环境下，民主政策的自主性是否还能存在。
• edg5000分享了个人经历，描述了从自建服务器到回归使用美国公司提供的LLM服务的转变，并预测未来AI将变得更廉价和普及，但需要时间。
• Synaesthesia乐观地认为，人们有能力共同创造想要的未来，AI有可能以目前无法想象的方式实现信息和智能的民主化。
• VikRubenfeld提出一个悖论：如果AI取代了大多数人类劳动，人们的收入将减少，从而无法购买AI生成的产品和服务，最终可能导致这种未来无法实现。
• daxfohl预期AGI在失控前会被阻止，认为当AGI对掌控者构成威胁时，相关方会采取行动防止灾难性后果。
• zugi对比了历史上其他重大技术发明，认为现在判断AI对经济权利的影响为时过早，AI有可能带来与目前设想相反的结果。

补充讨论：
• WillAdams提到Marshall Brain的小说《Manna》及历史上关于技术取代人力和再培训的讨论。
• andsoitis质疑是否只会存在一个AGI，还是多个AGI相互竞争。
• 0xbadcafebee反驳了关于AGI加剧不平等、削弱民主和导致技术封建主义的观点，认为不平等是政策选择的结果，而非AGI本身的问题，并质疑重新谈判经济框架的可行性。
• elcritch引用了Cobb-Douglas生产函数和相关研究，讨论AGI对经济权力的转移和就业的影响，并提出个体自给自足可能是一种避免最坏情况的方案。
• thangalin寻求对其AGI相关科幻书籍的反馈。
• slantaclaus建议通过像爱沙尼亚那样的数字投票应用增强民主参与。
• smitty1e好奇历史上是否有类似重新定义经济框架以公平分配AI繁荣的案例。
• warabe支持Yanis的技术封建主义理论，但希望看到更多实证研究。

争议焦点：
1. AGI是否会削弱民主政策的自主性，使人们成为被操控的工具。
2. AGI对经济不平等的影响程度及是否会导致技术封建主义。
3. 是否可能通过重新定义经济框架实现AI繁荣的公平分配。
4. AGI未来是单一主导还是多重竞争。

Title:

Abstract:
The rise of Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) marks an existential rupture in economic and political order, dissolving the historic boundaries between labor and capital. Unlike past technological advancements, AGI is both a worker and an owner, producing economic value while concentrating power in those who control its infrastructure. Left unchecked, this shift risks exacerbating inequality, eroding democratic agency, and entrenching techno-feudalism. The classical Social Contract-rooted in human labor as the foundation of economic participation-must be renegotiated to prevent mass disenfranchisement. This paper calls for a redefined economic framework that ensures AGI-driven prosperity is equitably distributed through mechanisms such as universal AI dividends, progressive taxation, and decentralized governance. The time for intervention is now-before intelligence itself becomes the most exclusive form of capital.

44475634.article_summary: 本文探讨了人工通用智能（AGI）崛起对经济和政治秩序的冲击。AGI作为既是劳动者又是所有者的角色，正在打破劳动与资本的传统界限，导致经济权力集中于控制其基础设施的少数人手中。这种转变可能加剧不平等，削弱民主机制，并巩固技术封建主义。为避免这种情况，必须重新谈判社会契约，建立新的经济框架，例如通过普遍AI红利、累进税制和去中心化治理，确保AGI带来的繁荣能够公平分配。干预的时机就是现在，以防止智能本身成为最排他的资本形式。
44475634.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AGI（人工智能通用智能）对社会、经济、民主和未来的潜在影响及相关争议

不同观点：
• jandrewrogers认为，AGI可能使大多数人无意识地成为被操控的工具（sock puppets），削弱民主政策反映人民真实意愿的能力。他质疑在AGI广泛应用的环境下，民主政策的自主性是否还能存在。
• edg5000分享了个人经历，描述了从自建服务器到回归使用美国公司提供的LLM服务的转变，并预测未来AI将变得更廉价和普及，但需要时间。
• Synaesthesia乐观地认为，人们有能力共同创造想要的未来，AI有可能以目前无法想象的方式实现信息和智能的民主化。
• VikRubenfeld提出一个悖论：如果AI取代了大多数人类劳动，人们的收入将减少，从而无法购买AI生成的产品和服务，最终可能导致这种未来无法实现。
• daxfohl预期AGI在失控前会被阻止，认为当AGI对掌控者构成威胁时，相关方会采取行动防止灾难性后果。
• zugi对比了历史上其他重大技术发明，认为现在判断AI对经济权利的影响为时过早，AI有可能带来与目前设想相反的结果。

补充讨论：
• WillAdams提到Marshall Brain的小说《Manna》及历史上关于技术取代人力和再培训的讨论。
• andsoitis质疑是否只会存在一个AGI，还是多个AGI相互竞争。
• 0xbadcafebee反驳了关于AGI加剧不平等、削弱民主和导致技术封建主义的观点，认为不平等是政策选择的结果，而非AGI本身的问题，并质疑重新谈判经济框架的可行性。
• elcritch引用了Cobb-Douglas生产函数和相关研究，讨论AGI对经济权力的转移和就业的影响，并提出个体自给自足可能是一种避免最坏情况的方案。
• thangalin寻求对其AGI相关科幻书籍的反馈。
• slantaclaus建议通过像爱沙尼亚那样的数字投票应用增强民主参与。
• smitty1e好奇历史上是否有类似重新定义经济框架以公平分配AI繁荣的案例。
• warabe支持Yanis的技术封建主义理论，但希望看到更多实证研究。

争议焦点：
1. AGI是否会削弱民主政策的自主性，使人们成为被操控的工具。
2. AGI对经济不平等的影响程度及是否会导致技术封建主义。
3. 是否可能通过重新定义经济框架实现AI繁荣的公平分配。
4. AGI未来是单一主导还是多重竞争。

data.title: Operators, Not Users and Programmers
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了消除“用户”和“程序员”之间区别的必要性，主张构建更具可塑性的软件系统，让普通用户也能轻松编程，而无需专门培训。文章以电子表格为例，强调其成功源于即时反馈和无缝部署。作者希望未来计算系统能兼具可塑性和技术稳定性，让编程像写简历一样简单。文中还探讨了现有可塑性系统，如WYSIWYG编辑器、浏览器开发工具和Sonic Pi等，指出它们提供了实时预览和无缝编辑功能，但缺乏如Git般复杂的版本控制。作者设想了一种无需事先批准即可使用和分享的系统，以增强用户的自主性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户与程序员之间的区别以及如何弥合这一差距，特别是在图形用户界面（GUI）和命令行界面（CLI）的环境中。

不同观点：
• jdp认为，CLI天然地将用户转变为程序员，因为每个命令都是可保存、修改和共享的程序。他质疑是否可以在GUI中实现类似的功能，例如命令历史的调用和修改。
• dustingetz引用Rich Hickey的观点，强调工具必须完全可被个人理解，才能激发创造力。他认为专家和初学者应使用相同工具，并将CLI与乐器类比。
• chubot支持将Unix shell演进为集成文本和图形的系统，认为文本界面不一定限于终端，并举例Excel和LibreCalc作为结合两种范式的例子。
• GianFabien指出，大型计算机公司倾向于迎合消费者而非程序员，通过消除易于访问的终端用户编程工具来实现，例如取消BASIC和HyperCard。
• rubyfan补充，企业环境中有意加剧这种分歧，IT部门通过控制用户可编程性来巩固管理角色。
• ppqqrr提到自己正在朝这一方向努力，并分享了一个相关链接。
• arduanika对这种方法表示赞赏，并期待看到更多发展。
• Jtsummers通过工作实例说明，允许终端用户自定义和修改系统可以促进协作，但需要合理的约束和保护措施。
• fellowniusmonk表示，个人项目可以很出色，但要使其生产就绪需要大量时间和资金。
• lmz认为，自动化有时是为了去除不可靠的人为因素。
• danparsonson强调，设计软件的困难在于处理每个决策的隐含意义，并指出并不是每个人都需要成为开发者。
• ginko对“消费者”这一标签持负面态度，认为无论是程序员还是用户，都应与计算机积极互动。
• michaelmrose进一步指出，人类的平均能力有限，开发易用软件并不意味着人人都会成为开发者。
• brundolf认为，AI可能是实现用户与程序员统一的最终途径，并指出这是计算历史的长期趋势。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于是否应通过工具统一用户和程序员，以及如何在易用性和功能性之间取得平衡。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是关于企业控制与用户自主权之间的张力，特别是在自定义和修改系统方面。
• AI作为潜在解决方案被提出，但也存在是否能真正实现的质疑。

44476166.article_content:
This post is part 0 of a multi-part series called
“the computer of the next 200 years”
.
the modern distinction between “programmers” and “users” is evil and destroys agency.
consider how the spreadsheets grow
🔗
spreadsheets are hugely successful. Felienne Hermans, who has spent her career studying spreadsheets,
attributes this success
to "
their immediate feedback system and their continuous deployment model
": the spreadsheet shows you its result as soon as you open it, and it requires no steps to run other than to install Excel and double-click the file.
Rik calls Excel “malleable software” and the resulting programs
“vine-like systems”
:
The dream of malleable software is that we can enlarge the space of possibilities, users can enjoy more freedom and get more out of their software, without having to rely on software developers to provide it for them.
i would go one step further: the dream of malleable software is to unify users and programmers, such that there are just “operators” of a computer, and “writing a program” doesn’t sound any harder than “writing a resume”:
the distinction between "user" and "programmer" is an artifact of our presently barely-programmable and barely-usable computing systems.  I would like to use the neutral word "operator" instead.
—
Stanislav
this is a relatively new distinction! if we look at the history of computing and of programming languages, we see very different patterns:
In the 1960’s the supply of programmers was not very deep so IBM and other companies trying to gain a computer sale would often have to sell the business prospect on the idea of creating its own programmer(s). Sometimes it was the shipping clerk; sometimes it was the head order taker; sometimes it was a bookkeeper, and sometimes it was a woman or man packing items in the warehouse.
—
Brian M. Kelly, The AS/400 and IBM i RPG Programming Guide
this is what i want: for programming to be easy and simple enough to pick up that people can do it without specialized training in the field, so that they can write
situated software
.
the “user/programmer” distinction
🔗
contrast malleable software to the systems that programmers often build:
Many, many technologists have taken one look at an existing workflow of spreadsheets, reacted with performative disgust, and proposed the trifecta of microservices, Kubernetes and something called a "service mesh".
This kind of Big Enterprise technology however takes away that basic agency of those Excel users, who no longer understand the business process they run and now have to negotiate with
ludicrous technology dweebs
for each software change. The previous pliability of the spreadsheets has been completely lost.
—
Cal Peterson
now, this doesn’t happen because programmers are stupid and evil. it happens because the systems we build are amenable to all the features that programmers
take for granted
:
distributed version control systems (VCS)
automated testing (when integrated with a VCS, often called "continuous integration")
gradual controlled rollouts (when integrated with a VCS, often called "continuous deployment")
what i want to imagine is what it would look like to build computing systems that have those features and are also malleable.
what could a malleable system with
low technical risk
look like?
🔗
let's start by looking at what malleable systems already exist.
malleable languages
🔗
spreadsheets, as previously discussed
WYSIWYG editors: Microsoft Word, Obsidian, Typst, Wordpress. In Word, and in Obsidian's default view, the compile step is completely hidden and it appears to the user as if the source and rendered view are the same. in other editors, the rendered view updates quickly and frequently enough that they get immediate feedback, just like a spreadsheet.
browser devtools, where editing an element in the inspector immediately updates the rendered view
sonic-pi
, where editing code live-updates the sound played
my blog
note these aren't
just
hot-patching, where you edit a system while it's running. hot-patching is certainly useful and i would like to see more of it, but it doesn't unify the source and rendered version of a program, you still have to trip the condition in order to observe the change. malleable languages are a combination of:
hot-patching
live previews that makes updates appear instant
undo/redo for the whole system
malleable version control
🔗
file shares: google drive; sharepoint; onedrive; etc. the tooling for diffing and reverting is very primitive compared to git or hg (in particular diffing is the responsibility of the application, not the VCS), but the primitives are there.
Bank Python
, where the distinction between local and persisted storage is smoothed over by the runtime
note a pattern here: these don't require prior approval in order to use. anyone can throw a file into google drive and hit share without prior approval (sometimes this is frowned upon, in which case it gets called "Shadow IT").
malleable deployment
🔗
Bank Python'

data.title: Eastern Baltic cod grow much smaller than they did due to overfishing
data.author: littlexsparkee
data.article_summary: 一项发表在《Science Advances》上的研究揭示，波罗的海东部鳕鱼因数十年过度捕捞而发生进化，体型显著缩小。过去，这些鳕鱼能长到超过三英尺长，但到2019年，它们的体型缩减了一半以上。研究分析了1996年至2019年间的152个鳕鱼耳石和DNA，发现与大体型相关的基因变异逐渐减少，表明过度捕捞改变了鳕鱼种群的遗传构成。尽管海洋温度升高也可能影响体型，但进化改变主要是人类活动所致。这种变化可能使物种更难适应未来环境变化，恢复需要很长时间，甚至可能无法实现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于波罗的海鳕鱼体型变化及其相关的生态、进化和保护问题

不同观点：
• ryao：认为放生小鱼可能导致“成年矮鱼”存活，破坏基因库，建议重新审视保护规则。
• olelele：强调波罗的海的污染问题，鱼类体内含有重金属和毒素，瑞典当局建议限制食用。
• rr808：提到毛利渔民曾选择食用中小型鱼，留下大型鱼作为优良繁殖者，但未提供具体参考。
• skeledrew：不同意将鳕鱼体型变小描述为主动行为，认为是“适者生存”的自然选择结果，大鳕鱼恢复需要很长时间。
• yard2010：将问题引申到蚊子，担心抗蚊措施会导致“超级蚊子”的出现，认为蚊子是比环境问题更紧迫的威胁。

补充讨论：
• littlexsparkee：指出原文标题过长，强调讨论内容仅限于波罗的海鳕鱼。
• lambdasquirrel：引用Philip Glass的交响乐句，表达对生态破坏的哀叹。
• weregiraffe：质疑按重量捕鱼时鱼的大小是否重要，认为一吨鳕鱼就是一吨鳕鱼。
• gouthamve：推荐一本关于鳕鱼捕捞历史的书，强调过度捕捞对鳕鱼数量的影响。
• ivanbalepin：提到有人收集波罗的海鳕鱼耳石，期待未来有新的利用方法。
• jongjong：认为进化可以在几代内快速发生，不一定要百万年，举例人类捕捞行为对鳕鱼体型的影响。
• thaumasiotes：提出传统解决方法是捕捞雄鱼，保留雌鱼，以避免性别选择导致繁殖问题，但雄鱼可能进化得更像雌鱼。
• PicassoCTs：建议在某些海域设置不可捕捞区，使用技术手段保护海洋生态。
• arusahni：简单感谢提供鳕鱼相关信息。
• macinjosh：询问是否存在传统养殖鳕鱼或DNA样本，建议使用基因技术恢复鳕鱼基因库。

争议焦点：
• 放生小鱼是否会破坏基因库（ryao与其他潜在支持放生者的观点对立）。
• 进化是否必须经过长时间（skeledrew与jongjong的快速进化观点的对立）。
• 保护措施的有效性和实施方式（PicassoCTs的激进保护建议与其他更温和建议的对立）。

44474759.article_content:
A catch of Baltic Sea cod in 1987 shows fish that grew more than three feet long, with Finnish fisheries biologist Eero Kalevi Aro.
Jesper Bay of the Danish Institute for Fisheries and Marine Research, March 1987
A new study reveals that decades of overfishing have altered the evolution of cod in the eastern Baltic Sea.
The research, published in the journal
Science Advances
on June 25, aimed to answer a question that had puzzled scientists for decades: What’s behind the dramatic size change in eastern Baltic cod?
Study lead author Kwi Young Han holds a fully grown cod in two hands.
Thorsten Reusch, GEOMAR
These fish used to be enormous. In 1996, the biggest Baltic cod grew more than three feet long. By 2019, however, their sizes had been cut in half, and the cod’s weight was but a fraction of its previous glory. Now, the average cod can sit in a person’s cupped hands.
For decades, fishers in the Baltic Sea caught cod relentlessly, using large nets. Smaller fish could escape more easily, presenting an external pressure to remain smaller. But directly connecting the population’s decrease in size to evolution—and not other environmental factors, such as pollution or temperature change—is notoriously difficult for scientists.
Regulators banned fishing of eastern Baltic cod in 2019 due to a population collapse, but their size still shows no signs of bouncing back. In the new study, scientists find that overfishing did not merely remove the biggest individuals—it changed the genetic composition of the cod population, predisposing them to remain small.
“Human harvesting elicits the strongest selection pressures in nature,”
Thorsten Reusch
, a marine ecologist at the GEOMAR Helmholtz Center for Ocean Research Kiel in Germany and co-author of the paper, tells Emily Anthes of the
New York Times
. “It can be really fast that you see evolutionary change.”
Did you know? Shrinking body size
In animals, shrinking body size is a known response to warming, with populations of
birds, frogs and mammals
reportedly growing to smaller sizes over time as climate change raises temperatures. Individual clownfish have been found to
shrink during ocean heat waves
.
To uncover the reason behind the dramatic drop in cod size, researchers analyzed 152 fish otoliths—tiny, bone-like structures found in the inner ear—that were collected from eastern Baltic cod harvested between 1996 and 2019. Otoliths can act as records of a fish’s annual growth, serving as biological timekeepers, like tree rings.
The researchers then sequenced the DNA of each fish and searched for areas of the genome and genetic variants that were associated with the growth rate. In the end, the team revealed that over time, variants related to a larger body size had become less common. This suggests an external pressure was guiding the cod’s evolution.
“What we are observing is evolution in action, driven by human activity,” Reusch tells the
Guardian
’s Hannah Devlin. “This is scientifically fascinating, but ecologically deeply concerning.”
Though warming ocean temperatures may also be a factor in driving smaller cod sizes, the dramatic decrease in size is far greater than what scientists expect could have been caused by temperature shifts alone, according to the
New York Times
.
Scientists say that this evolutionary change in cod can carry consequences. The genetic variants associated with a faster growth rate might already be lost from the population, according to a
statement
. This decrease in genetic diversity might make it harder for a species to adapt to environmental changes in the future.
“Evolutionary change unfolds over many generations,” says Reusch in the statement. “Recovery takes far longer than decline, and it may not even be possible.”
Stefano Mariani
, a marine biologist at Liverpool John Moores University in England who was not involved in the research, tells the
Guardian
the work is a “milestone” in showing that human activity can speed up evolution. This, he adds, highlights the importance of tracking not only a species’ numbers, but also its gene pool.

44474759.article_summary: 一项发表在《Science Advances》上的研究揭示，波罗的海东部鳕鱼因数十年过度捕捞而发生进化，体型显著缩小。过去，这些鳕鱼能长到超过三英尺长，但到2019年，它们的体型缩减了一半以上。研究分析了1996年至2019年间的152个鳕鱼耳石和DNA，发现与大体型相关的基因变异逐渐减少，表明过度捕捞改变了鳕鱼种群的遗传构成。尽管海洋温度升高也可能影响体型，但进化改变主要是人类活动所致。这种变化可能使物种更难适应未来环境变化，恢复需要很长时间，甚至可能无法实现。

不同观点：
• ryao：认为放生小鱼可能导致“成年矮鱼”存活，破坏基因库，建议重新审视保护规则。

• lambdasquirrel：引用Philip Glass的交响乐句，表达对生态破坏的哀叹。
• weregiraffe：质疑按重量捕鱼时鱼的大小是否重要，认为一吨鳕鱼就是一吨鳕鱼。

data.title: Stop Hiding My Controls: Hidden Interface Controls Are Affecting Usability
data.author: cxr
data.article_summary: 文章《Stop Hiding My Controls: Hidden Interface Controls Are Affecting Usability》探讨了隐藏界面控件对用户体验的影响。作者Philip Kortum援引Douglas Engelbart和Donald Norman的理论，区分了“外界知识”（界面控件可见，通过识别操作）和“内在知识”（用户需记忆控件和命令）。早期计算机如DOS系统依赖内在知识，而图形用户界面的下拉菜单将操作变为外界知识，降低了使用难度。然而，现代设备如智能手机又回到了依赖内在知识的模式，例如iPhone上的许多功能（如手电筒）需要用户记忆特定手势，没有明显提示，增加了使用难度。作者呼吁设计者应尽量使控件可见，以提升用户体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户界面（UI）设计中隐藏界面元素的合理性及影响

不同观点：
• BLKNSLVR：认为文章中的一些观点有待商榷，指出某些设计存在实际限制和成本考虑，例如车内物理旋钮的使用。同时提到一次不理想的用户体验，即一个应用中的开关标签与其功能不一致，导致困惑。
• weinzierl：理解为了利用屏幕空间而隐藏界面元素的做法，但质疑一些软件在隐藏元素后却不使用释放出来的空间，例如IntelliJ中的隐藏图标设计，认为这种做法缺乏合理性。
• WarOnPrivacy：以老式 Toyota 汽车为例，强调所有控制应始终可见、明确标记并易于操作。批评现代汽车隐藏关键控制（如钥匙孔和车内控制）的做法，认为这是对用户不友好的设计。
• nsriv：提到苹果移除实体Home键导致对年长用户解释交互变得更加困难，并指出安卓系统中3键导航的逐渐消失也对用户体验不利。
• zmmmmm：认为软件公司故意隐藏界面元素是为了锁定用户，特别是在软件达到用户饱和状态后，通过隐藏功能让用户习惯其生态系统，从而增加用户转移成本。
• userbinator：批评设计师为了美观而牺牲可发现性，认为这违背了让用户容易学习的设计原则，并将现代UI设计与飞机驾驶舱中明确的标签设计进行对比。
• padolsey：强烈同意隐藏界面元素影响无障碍设计，特别是对残疾人和老年用户，并认为这是趋势驱动下UI扁平化的结果，导致功能性下降。
• StellarScience：提到其团队的设计规则，要求键盘快捷键和上下文菜单必须通过清晰按钮或菜单可发现，虽然可能显得过时，但确保了可访问性，并批评Windows 11开始菜单移到屏幕中心的做法。
• analog31：补充了基于终端的UI也需要参考卡片来帮助记忆，认为这与早期GUI一样具有可发现性。
• temporallobe：抱怨车内音响系统将设置隐藏在多层菜单中且变灰不可用，导致困惑和不便。
• kulahan：以Discord为例，批评其隐藏按钮直到鼠标悬停才显示的做法，希望这种趋势停止。
• jofzar：质疑在网站没有移动端界面时讨论无障碍设计的合理性。
• eviks：指出当前“形式重于功能”的设计趋势，导致UI更注重美观而非实用性。
• rkagerer：抱怨安卓系统在点击时移动按钮位置，导致误点击，并预测广告商可能利用这种行为开发新的不良UI模式。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于现代UI设计中隐藏界面元素的合理性，一方认为这是为了美观和利用空间，另一方则认为这是对用户不友好且影响无障碍设计。
• 用户对现代汽车和软件中隐藏关键控制和功能的做法普遍表示不满，认为这增加了操作难度和困惑。
• 一些评论提到了UI设计的历史和演变，如早期终端UI和物理控制设备的设计，认为这些设计在可发现性和易用性方面有其优点。
• 还有对设计趋势的批评，认为当前的UI设计过于注重美观而忽视功能性和可访问性，导致用户体验下降。

Stop Hiding My Controls: Hidden Interface Controls Are Affecting Usability
Features
XXXII.4 July - August 2025
Page: 34
Digital Citation
Stop Hiding My Controls: Hidden Interface Controls Are Affecting Usability
Authors:
Philip Kortum
In the early 1960s, Douglas Engelbart [
1
] first introduced the notion of "knowledge in the world" versus "knowledge in the head" for computer interfaces—an idea that was later formalized and popularized by Donald Norman in his seminal book
The Psychology of Everyday Things.
From an interface design standpoint, knowledge in the world simply means that the controls you need are visible, and the identification and operation of these controls can be done through recognition rather than recall. Drop-down computer menus on modern graphical user interfaces, as shown in Figure 1, are a good example. Users don't have to memorize the command or even its specific location. Rather, they can browse through the menu command structure until they find the control they want to use.
Figure 1. Drop-down menus provide the user with knowledge in the world. It is clear what the user can do in this command window.
By contrast, knowledge in the head means that the user must memorize the necessary commands and controls for the operation of a specific device. In a bygone era many, if not most, computing tasks required significant knowledge in the head. You had to know the syntax or the command language to perform even rudimentary tasks. For example, determining what files were on your computer required you to have specific knowledge in the head to perform that task. If you were using a DOS-based system, you had to know the command was DIR, and that if you switched systems, the command was likely different. These kinds of systems were the ultimate hidden controls, as you needed to have complete knowledge in the head to accomplish anything (Figure 2).
Figure 2. A DOS command window. Without specific knowledge in the head, the user cannot perform a single action.
Insights
→
As interface complexity has increased, more controls are being hidden from the user.
→
While these hidden controls make the interface
look
easier to use, they actually make the interfaces much
harder
to use for novice users.
→
Designers need to make all controls visible in ways that maximize the user experience.
Human-computer interaction specialists quickly realized that requiring too much knowledge in the head prevented access to systems by a broad range of nonspecialist users. The birth of the drop-down menu system took us away from these hidden controls and put the knowledge into the world, allowing any user to identify which actions were available and then use the specific action they wanted. Much has been written about how this fundamental change altered and helped accelerate the adoption of computers [
2
]. With drop-down menus, people without specific, detailed training, and knowledge could access and use computers effectively and efficiently for a variety of new tasks that became attainable because of the new interface paradigm.
The birth of the drop-down menu system took us away from hidden controls and put the knowledge into the world.
Fast-forward 40 years and we are frequently reverting to a state where significant knowledge in the head is required to perform even rudimentary tasks on a computerized device. Of course, the form of the computer that we are using has changed drastically. Most desktop computers still adhere to the visible control model that was developed in the 1980s. Most of us, however, carry in our pocket a powerful handheld computer that is deceptively described as a phone, and this new computer demands that we have specific knowledge in the head. For example, if I want to activate the flashlight on my iPhone, I have to know to swipe up from the bottom left-hand corner in order to bring up a control panel where the flashlight button exists. There is absolutely nothing on the interface that indicates this is an available action. That might be fine if the action were intuitive or if it had some prominent affordance, but short of having read the iOS operation manual that is included in the box with the iPhone (oh, wait, no user manual is included in the box), there is no way to know this control exists. It is the quintessential hidden control—useful, lurking, and available—but only to those who know the trick. Want to see notifications on the iPhone? That's a separate hidden control, swiping down from the top corner this time. Apple Pay? Press an unlabeled, multifunction button twice. The number of hidden controls makes even simple operations difficult.
It's not just our phones that require this additional knowledge in the head. The other day I was locked out of my car. I had my keys, but the key fob button wouldn't work and neither would the litt

data.title: How to Network as an Introvert
data.author: agcat
data.article_summary: 这篇文章为内向者提供了有效的社交策略，帮助他们在活动中更好地建立联系。作者强调，内向者并非缺乏社交能力，而是需要适合自己的方法。准备阶段包括提前吃饭、穿戴一件易于引发话题的物品（“Whatzit”）、浏览新闻以备话题。进入活动时，通过暂停观察、保持开放的肢体姿势和延迟微笑来塑造良好的第一印象。开始对话时，避免肤浅的寒暄，使用“你大部分时间做什么？”等问题让对方敞开心扉。对话中，注意对方的小细节并适时回应。与主办方互动时，提供具体反馈并主动帮忙。离开时，有意识地道别，并在24小时内跟进联系，记录关键信息以便日后维护关系。最终，内向者无需强行改变自己，只需展示真实的自我即可成功社交。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何为社交焦虑者或内向者提供有效的社交建议，特别是在网络社交方面。

不同观点：

• boje：指出文章忽略了对为什么需要网络社交的基本解释，比如网络社交对建立和维持人际关系的重要性，并建议从心理健康和神经多样性角度讨论。

• konsalexee：提出不同文化背景下的社交差异，比如希腊和旧金山人在社交开场问题上的不同。
• GianFabien：分享了自己在社交活动中的经验，强调重复参加活动有助于建立联系，但要避免只和熟人交谈。

• nine_k：分享了自己使用的一些打破僵局的提问技巧，如询问对方当前的痴迷或令他们惊讶的事情。

- 一些评论者强调真诚和自然在社交中的重要性，而另一些则提供了具体的技巧和策略。

44475537.article_content:
How to Network as an Introvert
05 Jul, 2025
Why I am writing this?
Sometimes I’d leave an event unsure if I connected with anyone—or if anyone noticed I was there. I’d show up, blend in, talk just enough, smile just enough, and then disappear. The next morning, I’d wonder if anyone even remembered I was there.
This is what
often happens to introverts trying to network
. It’s not that we lack social skills. It’s that we’re playing the game without a system that fits our wiring.
I’m writing this blog as a reminder — a checklist for myself or anyone who relates — for the next professional gathering, party, or group event. A guide on what I now plan to do differently, step by step.
Before we begin: credit to the book
How to Talk to Anyone
by Leil Lowndes, which gave me this structure.
Before the event: shrink the unknowns
Walking into a room is easier when your nervous system isn’t in overdrive. Start with basics.
Eat before you go
. Most events are light on food and heavy on overstimulation. Being full helps you stay present, not preoccupied.
Add one small item to what you're wearing
that gives others something to comment on. It’s called a “Whatzit.” A pin, a vintage shirt, a random book in your hand. People need an excuse to start a conversation—give them one.
Scan the news for 2 minutes
. You don’t need to be a genius, but it keeps you from blanking out when someone says, “Did you see what happened today?” This isn’t about having talking points. It’s about removing friction.
Lastly, go over the
Six-Point Party Checklist
: Who’s going? When do you want to arrive? What’s the vibe? Why are you attending? Where is it exactly? How are you getting back? These simple questions give structure to an evening that often feels like chaos.
The moment you enter: control your signal
The most overlooked part of networking is the
first 5 seconds
. People scan you quickly and assign a story. You can shape that story.
Stand still in the doorway.Look around. Not like you're lost—like you're assessing. This pause signals confidence. Then pick a group that feels open and approach. No rush.
Keep your body open
. Wrists visible, arms uncrossed. Your posture is your pitch. Shoulders back, chin level.
Make eye contact before you smile. Let there be a beat. Then let the smile arrive slowly. This “delayed warmth” makes your smile feel specific, not generic. It’s subtle, but people feel the difference.
Opening lines: skip the small talk trap
Most people hate starting conversations because they overthink the words. The truth is, words are secondary. Your tone, posture, and energy do most of the work.
Start with:
“How do you spend most of your time?” Not “What do you do?”
It opens people up beyond job titles.
Listen for what lights them up. Echo a few of their words back to them. If someone says they’re working on solar hardware, ask, “Solar hardware?”—then pause. It gives them space to explain, and shows you’re actually listening.
When they’re done, don’t jump in with your story. Wait. Let the silence breathe. If you share something in common, wait a beat before you say it. The delay makes it feel like insight, not interruption.
Mid-conversation: be the one who tracks
Keep track of the small things
. Their dog’s name. The town they just moved from. That one thing they said in passing.
If you’re in a group, use their own story to spotlight them. Say something like, “You have to tell everyone about that glacier trip.” That line alone can shift how they remember you. It shows that you’re paying attention—and willing to share the room.
If the conversation stalls, don’t panic. Repeat the last few words they said with a slight upward tone. It’s called “parroting,” and it gently invites them to keep going without forcing anything.If someone says, “Work’s been kind of chaotic lately,” you can just respond with, “Chaotic lately?”—and let them take it from there.
Engaging the host: go specific, not loud
Hosts are often moving fast. Don’t waste their time with “Great party.” Say something more vivid. “The lighting is perfect.” “Everyone feels relaxed.” It anchors your presence with detail.
Offer to help with something small
—refill ice, carry extra plates. Tiny acts give you visibility without performance.
Leaving well: be memorable, not dramatic
Don’t disappear. Say goodbye with intention. Use an uncommon adjective: “Had a remarkable time.” “Such a thoughtful gathering.” That small twist makes you stick.
If you connected with someone,
follow up within 24 hours
. Share an article, a meme, a line that ties back to your conversation. This isn’t networking. It’s reinforcement.
Write down what you remember
—glacier, dog name, their startup idea. Those notes are your memory system for real relationships.
Three weeks later, check in. It’s not needy. It’s respectful. Most people forget. You didn’t. That matters.
Closing thoughts
What i have learnt is that you don’t need to work the room or become someone you’re not. Most of the time, it’s enough to show u

data.article_summary: 本文主要描述了myNoise网站创始人遭遇黑客攻击的经历。攻击者试图注入代码失败后，转而反复下载音频文件，浪费带宽。这使创始人感到沮丧，因为他的网站致力于创造一个积极的网络空间，而这种破坏行为让他不得不耗费时间和精力来防御攻击，而非创造新内容。尽管黑客未能使服务器崩溃，但他们偷走了创始人的时间、精力和内心的平静。文章还提到创始人通过种树等行动努力抵消网站能耗，并分享了一个救助小鸽子的故事，表达了对建设与破坏不平衡的感慨。最终，创始人决定继续坚持自己的理想，种植树木、制作声音、帮助小动物，并维持myNoise作为一个和平的避风港。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• drpixie和iwassayinbourns认为，这类攻击（扫描/探测）在互联网上很常见，主要是自动化工具所为，建议不要个人化看待，并提出技术解决方案，如使用Fail2ban或其他速率限制工具来保护服务器。

• mathiaspoint则持冷静态度，认为这是互联网上的常态，建议不必过于紧张或个人化看待。

• BLKNSLVR认为虽然世界充满挑战和不公，但继续创造和建设是唯一可行的道路，强调面对困难时的坚持和积极心态。

• Pine_Mushroom和xyst提到对域名被盗或内容被爬取的类似经历，认为低价值域名被盗令人困惑，并猜测攻击可能来自大型公司或自动化工具，而非个人攻击者。
• smoll和orourke对受害者的遭遇表示同情，并强调这种经历可能激发出更强的决心和清晰的人生目标。

This blog helps me stay in touch with all of you who support the myNoise project. The website only exists because of your contributions. You all are incredible! I'll be happy to share some "behind the scenes" stories here, and more pictures
there
. Keep in mind that English is not my native language, and will probably be the only thing that sounds bad on this site ;-)
What a Hacker Stole From Me
July 4, 2025 •
I’ve always dreamed of offering a small slice of utopia on the Internet; a place I would love to visit myself. You all know by now, myNoise is my attempt to build something positive, in a world that often feels too chaotic.
A couple of days ago, someone (or some entity) tried to attack this website. They sent hundreds of thousands of requests, attempting to inject code into the site. That didn’t work. myNoise isn’t built on a conventional CMS; I wrote everything from scratch. Maybe that helped. But then they changed strategy. They began downloading every single sound file, again and again. Wasting precious bandwidth, just for the sake of it.
I try to be mindful about my footprint, and the footprint of my noises. Every year, I plant trees to offset the energy used by visitors on the site. I don’t talk much about it anymore, because over the years, it has triggered some criticism. And yes, I agree that the methodology can be questioned. But the idea behind it is simply this: trying to behave responsibly.
And then someone comes along and deliberately floods the server. Just to waste. I guess everyone feels the same when faced with an act of vandalism. That’s the deep unfairness, rooted in the law of entropy: it always takes less energy to break something than it took to create it.
Lately, I find this harder and harder to accept that. Maybe it has something to do with my health incident two years ago. I saw how quickly and easily a disease can take hold of your body, and how long and how much effort it takes to recover. The universal law of entropy again. But illness, most of the time, is not caused by anyone. So we accept it and fight. But when harm is caused by another human being, on purpose, it leaves a different feeling.
Yes, of course, there are worse things in life than someone trying to exhaust a server. This blog post isn’t really about that attack. It was just the trigger to the melancholy that I am filled with now. The reminder of something larger: the imbalance between building and destroying, the rigged combat between the good and the bad. How the world seems to get crazier every day… or maybe it’s always been this way, and I’m just getting older.
Not long ago, we found a young pigeon that had fallen from its nest and had been severely injured. We fed him with a syringe for weeks. We cared for him like family—well, with my family name, I can say we are family. Now he flies freely around the neighborhood, but still comes back to visit us. These are the things that makes me happy. The satisfaction of making small positive changes.
But even here, I can't now refrain from imagining myself there might be someone in the neighborhood who doesn’t like birds. Someone who might one day destroy what we tried hard to save.
It might sound unrelated to server attacks—but to me, it is. It is the same melancholy that visits me sometimes.
That hacker didn’t manage to bring the server down. But still, they did steal something from me. My time and energy. And what little zennitude I had left (my wife would tell you I don’t have much to begin with - haha). So yes, if they’re keeping score, they can mark this as a success. Time I had planned to spend making new sounds, shaping quiet ambiences, working on something positive and useful. Instead, I spent it trying to understand what was happening, how to stop it, and how to protect the project from future attacks. Time lost in defense—something that wouldn’t be needed in my utopian world.
But I’ve made a choice. I’ll keep planting trees. I’ll keep making sounds. I’ll keep helping baby pigeons. I’ll keep offering that little shelter of peace that is myNoise, for

data.article_summary: 7-Zip 25.00版本发布，主要更新包括：支持使用超过64个CPU线程进行压缩，并在多处理器组之间分配线程；bzip2压缩速度提升15-40%；deflate压缩速度提升1-3%；改进对zip、cpio和fat档案的支持；修复了一些漏洞和安全问题。用户反应积极，多人表示支持和赞赏。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：7-Zip及其他压缩工具的功能、使用场景及不足

不同观点：
• Dwedit认为7-Zip 15.05版本在今天仍然有用，因为它是最后一个内置支持NSIS安装脚本反编译的版本，之后的版本因安全问题移除了该功能。
• Ofek提到有另一个项目通过添加对多种编解码器（如Zstandard）的支持来跟踪7-Zip的上游更新，并表示自己和其他人更倾向于使用该项目的发布版本。
• Gertop抱怨7-Zip不支持像WinRAR那样直接浏览.tar.gz文件，而必须先将.tar提取到临时文件，这对于处理大文件来说不方便，尤其是与WinRAR的处理方式对比后显得更不高效。
• Jainilprajapati质疑现在是否还需要额外的压缩工具，因为Windows已经内置了zip功能。
• Pregnenolone希望RAR或7-Zip能实现一个内存密集型的KDF（密钥派生函数）用于加密档案。
• Shmerl表示最近使用zstd和tar组合来创建能保留文件元数据的档案。
• Doctorpangloss提出一个问题，为什么Windows不预装解压缩工具。

补充讨论：
• 关于7-Zip对特定文件格式（如.tar.gz）处理方式的不足与改进期望。
• 用户对压缩工具功能（如加密、元数据保留）的进一步需求。
• 不同工具（如7-Zip、WinRAR、自定义项目）在特定使用场景中的优劣对比。
• 对操作系统内置功能（如Windows的zip支持）的讨论以及是否足够满足用户需求。

争议焦点：
• 7-Zip在处理特定文件格式（如.tar.gz）时的效率问题成为用户抱怨的焦点，尤其是与WinRAR对比时显得不够便捷。
• 用户对压缩工具是否仍然必要存在不同看法，部分用户认为Windows内置功能已足够，而其他用户则寻求更多功能和改进。

data.title: The Right Way to Embed an LLM in a Group Chat
data.author: kenforthewin
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了在群聊中嵌入AI助手的利弊，特别是在专用应用如旅行规划app **TripJam**中的使用。在普通群聊中，AI助手可能偶尔有用，但也会打断对话。然而，当AI被赋予访问工具的权限时，例如在群聊中创建投票，它会更加实用，节省手动操作时间。

在像**TripJam**这样的专用应用中，AI助手通过执行特定任务（如搜索餐厅、添加地点、创建投票等）变得非常有用。这些功能通过一系列工具调用实现，如`add_location`、`center_map`、`search_places`等，帮助用户高效规划行程。

为了避免打扰用户，AI只在被明确询问时回应，并计划未来通过分析聊天内容主动提示用户可能的AI功能，同时确保AI操作结果而非整个对话对群组可见。文章还提到在大型群聊中，不必将所有历史聊天发给AI，以提高效率。

总结：在专用群聊应用中，嵌入AI助手通过执行具体任务提升用户体验，但需谨慎设计以避免打扰用户。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在群聊中的应用及其优缺点

不同观点：
• **femto**：认为AI在群聊中生成的回应往往是无用的噪音，建议AI应按照要求简洁地完成任务，例如生成投票。同时，AI应明确标识，让用户知道自己在与AI互动，而非普通用户。

• **MongooseStudios**：对将LLM加入群聊持强烈反对态度，甚至表示如果朋友这样做，会考虑结交新朋友。这表明对LLM介入个人社交圈的高度抵触。

• **cryptozeus**：质疑AI生成大量无背景信息的建议的价值，认为用户仍需自行筛选和判断，违背了使用AI简化决策的初衷。用户更倾向于通过UI和图像等直观数据做决策。

• **bearjaws**：认为图像生成可能是LLM在聊天中唯一有趣的应用，但速度太慢，难以在快速变化的对话中保持相关性。举例说明在特定场景（如体育博彩群）中图像生成的实际应用。

• **mmoustafa**：对文章表示赞赏，认为其涵盖了在构建群聊机器人时所需考虑的各个方面，显示出对文章内容的认同。

• **dovys**：对非操作系统自带的LLM在私人消息中的应用表示不信任，强调对安全和隐私的关注。

• **renewiltord**：认为在特定情况下，群聊中有一个可以共同使用的助手是有用的，但不希望它干扰正常的聊天 flow。强调助手在临时性讨论中的价值。

• **leakycap**：明确反对将LLM嵌入群聊，认为这是不合适的。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于LLM在群聊中的实用性和干扰性。支持者认为在特定场景下有价值，反对者则担心其对正常社交互动的干扰和隐私问题。
• 标识LLM身份的建议被提出，以增加透明度和用户信任。
• 对AI生成内容的质量和相关性存在质疑，用户更倾向于直观和易于理解的建议形式。

44476084.article_content:
In a typical group chat, adding an AI assistant may be occasionally useful at best, and downright annoying at worst. If a user has a question for an AI related to the discussion, it isn’t much more effort to switch to a different app like ChatGPT and, if needed, copy the answer back to the group chat. Having AI embedded into the chat might save a step or two, but at the cost of potentially derailing the existing conversation.
AI gets a bit more useful when you give it access to embedded tools. If your chat supports polls, for example, you could ask the AI to look up potential restaurants for a weekend hangout and create a poll for the group to vote on. If you relied on an external app like ChatGPT to do this research, you’d have to manually set up the poll and copy in the restaurant context, so you’ve just saved yourself a lot of time.
Where AI-assisted group chat becomes incredibly useful is in the context of a
purpose-built chat embedded in a larger application
. Our use case is a travel planning app,
TripJam
, where travel groups collaborate on their itinerary, to-dos, budget, and more.
TJ searches Google for restaurant ideas and adds them as poll options for the group to vote on.
What’s the Problem?
In an app like ChatGPT, the basic intent of each message is clear: the user is addressing the AI and expects a response. In the context of a group chat, however, an AI assistant’s job is much more difficult: the average message is more likely than not directed at another user, so the AI’s goal should be to respond only when needed and otherwise be unobtrusive.
In an app like TripJam, the assistant is only useful to the extent that it can perform the action asked of it. This action may be as simple as summarizing a potential vacation location, or a complex multi-step process such a looking up top restaurants in an area, moving the map to display them next to the other itinerary locations, and adding them to the itinerary itself. Interaction with the assistant should feel like time-saving magic, and as soon as that usefulness breaks down, the user will be much less likely to interact with the AI in the future.
TJ can add locations to the itinerary, interact with the map, and highlight the location it's referring to.
Tool Use
The AI assistant should have an extensive list of tools available to interact with your system. A modern LLM can chain these function calls together in ways that feel seamless and save users time and effort.
Available Functions
add_location
Description:
Add an event and corresponding location to the trip’s itinerary. Location editing and deletion also supported.
Arguments:
name, description, date_time, lat, lng
center_map
Description:
Move the map view to the coordinates specified.
Arguments:
lat, lng, zoom
search_places
Description:
Search for recommended locations in an area using the Google Places API.
Arguments:
lat, lng, search_term, radius
add_todo
Description:
Add a todo item to the trip’s todo list.
Arguments:
title, description, assigned_to_id
add_poll
Description:
Create a poll to help the group make decisions.
Arguments:
name, options
System Prompt
In a purpose-built group chat app, the
system prompt
can provide valuable context about app state and user data.
Aside from guiding how the AI should behave, TripJam injects trip-specific info directly into the prompt, like the itinerary, list of users, and the requesting user’s name and timezone. Compared to requiring the AI to fetch this context through function calls, injecting it ensures the AI always has the necessary info, especially when adding a location to the itinerary.
Querying the AI
How do we parse user intent in regards to the AI assistant? For v1 we opted for a conservative approach: the AI will only respond when the user queries it directly, either by prefixing a message with the assistant’s name (“TJ, what are some popular restaurants in Manhattan?”) or by flagging a chat message to be sent to the AI after the fact. In either case, the entire group sees the message that’s sent to the AI as well as its response.
We plan to enhance this behavior in a couple ways. First, our current approach requires the users to already be aware of the AI features available to them in the group chat. Instead, we could attempt to infer AI intent based on the contents of the chat, and prompt users to request AI assistance. We need to be careful here to avoid annoying our users (think Clippy).
Another planned enhancement: not every message sent to the AI needs to be visible to the entire group. For example, if a user requests that the AI perform a simple action such as adding a location, only the result of that action needs to be visible to the group (the actual location added), not the entire AI conversation. This is reminiscent of more traditional actions in group chat applications like slash commands in Slack.
Context
Group chats can become very large, so it quickly becomes unfeasible to send the entire chat history to the AI assistant

data.title: WinUAE 6 Amiga Emulator
data.author: doener
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要介绍了自定义芯片组模拟的重大更新。芯片组模拟（Agnus/Alice 和 Denise/Lisa）几乎完全重写，实现了内部周期精确。Denise/Lisa 模拟现在运行于单独线程，大幅提升精确模式性能。VPOSW/VHPOSW 技巧和同步信号等现在都实现了周期精确模拟，支持硬连线和编程混合模式。显示和计数器独立模拟，支持无限次前后移动。所有屏幕模式现在都能正确计算显示高度，包括处理多次修改。新增低层次键盘模拟，支持三种键盘微控制器变体和NKRO选项。此外，还合并了PCI设备和Voodoo 3模拟更新，修复了多个问题，如Prometheus FireStorm PCI桥接和GDI模式资源释放等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Amiga相关软件和模拟器的开源以及用户体验问题

不同观点：
• [关于开源的期望] sillywalk 表示希望 Kickstart ROMs 和 Amiga OS 的源代码能够开源发布。他提到自己已经购买过一份拷贝，但似乎认为这并不足够，隐含了对开放源代码的支持，可能出于对软件保护、修改或保存历史的目的。

• [对模拟器用户体验的关注] jonwinstanley 并没有直接回应开源话题，而是关注于 winUAE 模拟器的用户体验（UX）。他回忆起过去使用 winUAE 时的困惑，特别是需要选择特定的 Amiga 型号和模拟磁盘加载过程。他希望能够更快速、简单地启动和运行他曾经喜欢的旧 Amiga 游戏，暗示了对用户友好性改进的期待。

补充讨论：
• [winUAE 的复杂性] jonwinstanley 提到过去的 winUAE 版本操作复杂，需要用户对 Amiga 硬件和软件有较多了解，这可能阻碍了只想玩游戏的普通用户。他关心的核心在于模拟器的简化操作和易用性。

• [潜在的争议焦点] 虽然 sillywalk 关心的是软件开源问题，而 jonwinstanley 关心用户体验，但两者之间可能存在的争议焦点是：开源是否能够改善用户体验。开源社区的开发者或许能够通过开放源代码来简化模拟器的使用流程，但 jonwinstanley 的评论暗示出对当前开源或技术解决方案在易用性方面的疑虑。

• [历史软件保存与实际使用的冲突] sillywalk 的评论还隐含了一种历史保存与实际使用之间的张力。他购买过软件拷贝，但现在希望这些老旧系统能够开源，这反映了老用户在保存历史和实际使用（如通过模拟器）之间寻求平衡的心态。

44475600.article_content:
Major update to custom chipset emulation. Internally almost everything in main chipset emulation has been rewritten.
Fastest possible/JIT mode chipset timing/sync had major changes which can cause side-effects.
Bugs are very possible, especially in very rarely used features.
Custom chipset rewrite
Custom chipset emulation (Agnus/Alice and Denise/Lisa) almost completely rewritten. Almost every part of chipset emulation is now internally cycle accurate.
Custom chipset Denise/Lisa emulation is now running in separate thread for large performance increase in accurate emulation modes compared to previous versions.
VPOSW/VHPOSW tricks are now cycle-accurately emulated without restrictions.
Horizontal and vertical blanking and sync start/end, csync, csync equalization pulses, etc are now fully cycle-accurately emulated, both hardwired and programmed. Mixing of hardwired and programmed is fully supported. Agnus/Alice hardwired PAL/NTSC sync generator is almost logic gate level emulated.
“Display” and Agnus/Alice vertical and horizontal counters are now fully separately emulated, display emulation now works correctly even if Agnus vertical or horizontal is moved backwards or forwards or anywhere (even outside of normal display range), unlimited times per line and/or field.
All screenmodes (including “Fake” NTSC or similar mode) now count total number of “display” lines and uses it to setup display height. These modes now work even if they do multiple V(H)POSW modifications.
Interlace detection now uses vsync timing like real displays.
BPLCON0 ERSY=1 without connected genlock sync stop timing is now accurate. This was faked previously.
Full AGA hires/shres bitplane and sprite horizontal granularity support. Separate subpixel mode does not exist anymore.
ECS Agnus/AGA UHRES bitplane and sprite RGA DMA slots (0x78, 0x7a) emulated. Completely useless feature because UHRES can only do some DMA transfers to nowhere. It needs extra hardware that was never implemented. UHRES needs to be emulated because (possibly accidentally enabled) UHRES DMA can steal cycles from copper, blitter and CPU.
NTSC LOL (long line) state is accurately emulated. Mismatched STRLONG strobe and LOL state now causes correct lores pixel wide horizontal shift. (Mismatched = for example CPU writing to STRLONG when line is not long)
Blitter channel sequencer should be 100% accurate now, except possibly line to non-line mid operation switch. Blitter “micro-operation” timings are not yet 100%: when exactly it applies A shift, B shift etc. This will be tested and implemented in the future. Only affects blitter result if BLTxDAT/shifts/etc are modified mid-blit. Channel enable/fill mode/desc/minterm/BLTxMOD/BLTxPT mid-blit changes should be already fully accurate.
Collision emulation is now very fast. Collision mode default changed to Full collision.
Ultra extreme debug mode now shows normally hidden bitplane and sprite pixels inside horizontal and vertical blanking periods. Previously only background color was fully visible.
DMA debugger has much more detailed information available.
Other new features
Low level keyboard emulation. Emulates keyboard microcontroller internal ROM code and keyboard matrix, optionally with or without NKRO. All 3 keyboard MCU variants supported. (CSG 6570-036, 68HC05C and D8039HLC. 6500-1 used in A1000 keyboards is same as 6570-036 but with older ROM code. 6500-1 ROM is not yet dumped). Caps lock led state is fully emulated in low level keyboard emulation modes, including demos that flash caps lock led. Chipset panel “Keyboard connected” checkbox replaced with Keyboard mode (“Disconnected”, “UAE high level keyboard” and list of different low level emulated keyboard models)
PCI Matrox Millennium, Millennium II, Mystique and Mystique 220 emulation from 86box (originally from PCem)
Merged Voodoo 3 emulation updates from 86box.
Added 512kWOM A1000 512k WOM expansion emulation. Option in Expansions->Built-in expansions.
Added RIPPLE IDE controller emulation.
Fixes
Prometheus FireStorm PCI bridge PCI IO mapping fixed.
Fixed Mediator 1200TX second PCI window mapping logic.
Fixed TekMagic onboard RAM config type.
Do not reject (reject = not hardware accelerated, lets Picasso96 software fallback to handle it) uaegfx Picasso96 blit operation if RenderInfo BytesPerRow field is zero. Zero BPR is allowed.
GDI mode didn’t free all resources when switching between native and RTG mode.
If selected graphics API is not supported, test all other options. Previously failing D3D9 switched to GDI, even if D3D11 was available.
Fast/non-accurate emulation mode and writing to CIA high timer register didn’t load timer from latch immediately in oneshot mode if timer was already running (Introduced in 4.9.x)
uaegfx RTG vertical blank interrupt might have been duplicated or lost in some situations (very old bug), depending on RTG panel refresh rate setting.
Passthrough printing mode fix for v4+ Windows printer drivers.
Fixed FDI disk image support.
JIT FPU

• [对模拟器用户体验的关注] jonwinstanley 并没有直接回应开源话题，而是关注于 winUAE 模拟器的用户体验（UX）。他回忆起过去使用 winUAE 时的困惑，特别是需要选择特定的 Amiga 型号和模拟磁盘加载过程。他希望能够更快速、简单地启动和运行他曾经喜欢的旧 Amiga 游戏，暗示了对用户友好性改进的期待。

补充讨论：
• [winUAE 的复杂性] jonwinstanley 提到过去的 winUAE 版本操作复杂，需要用户对 Amiga 硬件和软件有较多了解，这可能阻碍了只想玩游戏的普通用户。他关心的核心在于模拟器的简化操作和易用性。

data.article_summary: 《Tetra Master》是《最终幻想IX》中的一款可选卡牌小游戏。尽管初看类似《最终幻想VIII》中的Triple Triad，但即便玩上百场，单凭游戏内的教程仍难以完全掌握规则。文章作者在深入研究后发现，游戏内及手册中均未提供完整规则，导致玩家困惑。文章详细探讨了Tetra Master的规则、卡牌获取、随机性及对战机制，并指出需查阅外部资料才能全面理解。尽管如此，作者强调《最终幻想IX》本身仍是一款令人享受的游戏，卡牌小游戏并非主线必需，因此不会严重影响整体体验。最终，作者建议深入理解规则以提升游戏乐趣。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕《Final Fantasy》系列中的小游戏（尤其是Tetra Master）的游戏设计及其随机性和不确定性的讨论。

不同观点：
• **jokoon的观点**：认为隐藏规则和随机性是故意设计的游戏元素。这种设计增加了不确定性，类似于赌博游戏，防止玩家制定出始终有效的策略，从而保持游戏的悬念。jokoon指出，玩家感到沮丧是因为他们期望能够提前确定结果，成为游戏专家。而加入随机性是一种聪明的设计，能避免玩家总是能够预测胜负。

• **musicale的观点**：对Tetra Master的规则和设计表示欣赏，提到其复杂性和不确定性是游戏特色，甚至引用Square Enix曾推出的线上版本和粉丝项目。同时，musicale认为Triple Triad（来自《Final Fantasy VIII》）相对更简单和易玩，并将其与Tetra Master进行对比，表达了对前者的偏爱。

• **jasonephraim的观点**：分享个人体验，提到自己在《Final Fantasy IX》中的小游戏Tetra Master一直感到困惑，即便在多年后重新游玩《Final Fantasy IX》的Switch版本，依然对游戏规则感到不解。

补充讨论：
• **关于游戏规则的透明度**：jokoon和musicale的观点中都涉及到游戏规则的复杂性和不透明性。jokoon认为这种设计是有意的，而musicale则欣赏这种复杂性，并提到其他类似游戏的对比。

• **关于玩家体验和期望**：jokoon提到玩家期望能够掌握游戏并成为专家，而随机性和不确定性打破了这种期望，可能导致挫败感。jasonephraim的亲身经历验证了这种挫败感，即便多年后重新体验游戏，依然对规则感到困惑。

• **关于不同小游戏的对比**：musicale明确对比了Tetra Master和Triple Triad，认为后者更简单和易玩，这种对比提供了一个不同的视角，显示出玩家对游戏复杂度和设计偏好的多样性。

争议焦点：
• 随机性和不确定性是否是好的游戏设计选择。jokoon认为是聪明的设计，而从jasonephraim的体验来看，这种设计可能导致玩家的困惑和挫败感。这表明玩家对随机性和不确定性的接受程度存在差异。

The Hell of Tetra Master
2025-07-02
This article is a translation, the
original version is
available here
.
Tetra Master
is the optional card game in
Final Fantasy IX
. At first glance, it seems similar to
Triple Triad
— the card game from Final Fantasy VIII. And while you can develop a general intuition for how to win, especially if you have strong cards, after playing over a hundred matches, I had to admit something: just playing the game and reading all the
in-game
tutorials wasn’t enough to truly understand the rules. Eventually, I gave in and started looking things up to figure out what I was missing. The complete absence of
any actual rules
— whether in the game or the manual — left me utterly frustrated, which is what led me to write this article, illustrated in OCaml.
Context
Simple, but not in every aspect
Discovering the Rules Online
The Tetra Master
Cards in the Story
Collecting Cards
A Brief Note on Randomness
The Rules According to the Manual
Challenging an Opponent
Basic Rules
Winning a Card
Rewards and Penalties
Card Limit and Menu
Conclusion from Reading the Manual
Detailed Rules
Game Board
Simple Card Capture
Battle
Multiple Battles
Card Anatomy
Reading a Card’s Statistics
Interpreting Hexadecimal Statistics
Battle Progression: Even More Randomness
Calculating the Probability of Winning a Duel
Combos
Pre-conclusion on the Rules
Experience and Card Evolution
Evolution of Attack and Defense
Evolution of Card Types
Card List
Collector Level
The Different Levels
On the distinction between cards
Points awarded per card
Note on Pattern Permutations
The cherry on top
To conclude, finally
What can we take away from this?
The Next Part
Acknowledgments
The Final Word
Just to be clear, my salty critique
is aimed solely at the Tetra
Master card game
. While I can fully understand (and even agree with)
some of the criticisms directed at the ninth entry in the series, I
personally enjoyed the game a lot — maybe out of nostalgia. And since
the card game isn't required to progress through the main story, it's
entirely possible to enjoy the game while carrying only a mild sense
of frustration at not grasping the intricate — and arguably
unguessable — mechanics of its ruleset.
Some people will probably find it pretty strange to revisit this game
more than 22 years
after its European release... and honestly,
they’re not wrong! I have to admit, I find it quite amusing to try and
turn this website into
a sort of dusty old library
, filled with
useless knowledge
.
Context
I discovered the
Final
Fantasy
series through
its seventh installment in the late ’90s, watching my cousin Thomas
play it with rapt attention. I was deeply impressed and quickly became
a big fan of the series for its atmosphere, music, and stories. That
said, being very young at the time and having only played
JRPGs
like Pokémon Red, I didn’t care much about game mechanics — which
might sound awful to you, as I was missing out on what truly makes a
video game
a
game — so I rarely read the tutorials and just
focused on progressing through the story.
Even though the Final Fantasy series — at least the entries released
in Europe at that time — isn’t known for being particularly
difficult, ignoring the understanding of systems like the
materia
system in Final Fantasy VII
can make progressing through the adventure
very challenging
. And
yes, while Final Fantasy VI, VII, VIII, and IX have a similar
Skill Ceiling
to
Pokémon Red and Blue, I have a feeling that the
Skill
Floor
for those three
Final Fantasy games is significantly higher.
Holding a fondness for these games I had
never
finished, years
later I decided to play them again with the goal of completing
them. At that time, as a programmer, my interest was focused on the
RPGMaker
series — a
toy software
for
building RPGs that offers a programming interface to create original
systems and grants great customization freedom for
advanced
users
. Playing classics from the
genre seemed like a perfect way to learn!
Since
JRPGs
are often long games and I wasn’t playing like a
hardcore gamer, nearly 10 years later, after finishing FF6, FF7, and
FF8, my takeaway was clear:
reading the tutorials and understanding
the various game mechanics makes the experience much easier
. While
each of these entries has its own subtle complexities related more to
the
Skill Ceiling
, overall the games were quite simple — which isn’t
a criticism — and I was ready to dive into FF9 with confidence.
Simple, but not in every aspect
Like its predecessors, Final Fantasy IX isn’t a complicated game. The
mechanics are easy to grasp, and although battles can sometimes feel
slow-paced — and the
Trance
system can be frustrating if you’re coming from the previous two games
— it’s pretty clear how to be effective quickly. My frustration,
however, comes from the card game. Like its predecessor, the game
includes an
ad-hoc
system called
Tetra Master
, which is
introduced fairly early in the story. As a player, I’m generally quite
supportiv

data.author: dionhaefner
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了如何使用Tesseract-JAX库进行基于有限元仿真的参数化形状优化。主要内容包括：

1. 构建包含可微有限元求解器的Tesseract。
2. 使用有限差分方法使非自动微分几何操作（如计算3D模型的有符号距离场）可微分。
3. 通过Tesseract-JAX组合多个Tesseract，创建可微形状优化管道。
4. 使用optax进行基于梯度的优化。

文章详细说明了如何通过自动微分（AD）对设计变量进行优化，以提升设计性能。优化问题被公式化为最小化结构的合规性，通过Tesseract模块化和AD特性，实现高效的参数化形状优化。文章还介绍了如何设置和构建所需的Tesseract镜像及相关代码示例。

44453814.article_content:
Parametric shape optimization with differentiable FEM simulation
¶
Note
All examples are expected to run from the
examples/<example_name>
directory of the
Tesseract-JAX repository
.
In this example, you will learn how to:
Build a Tesseract that wraps a differentiable finite-element solver from
jax-fem
.
Build a Tesseract that uses finite differences under the hood to enable differentiability of a non-autodifferentiable geometry operation (computing a signed distance field from a 3D model).
Compose both Tesseracts with Tesseract-JAX to create a pipeline that can be used for differentiable shape optimization.
Perform gradient-based optimization using
optax
on the Tesseract-JAX pipeline.
Introduction
¶
In this notebook, we explore the optimization of a parametric structure made of a linear elastic material. The structure is parametrized by N bars, each of which has M piecewise linear segments. We seek the ideal configuration of the
\(y\)
-coordinates of the vertices that connect those bar segments. This notebook is based on the
2D topology optimization example
from
jax-fem
, but we solve the problem using a parametric approach instead.
That is, we use end-to-end automatic differentiation (AD) through several components to optimize the design variables directly with respect to (simulated) performance of the design.
The design space is defined using a geometry library called PyVista, which does not support automatic differentiation. However, we can enable differentiability of this operation by using a finite difference approximation of the Jacobian matrix.
We denote the design space as a function
\(g\)
that maps the design variables to a signed distance field. Then, we can then define the density field
\(\rho(\mathbf{x})\)
as a function of a signed distance field (SDF) value
\(g(\mathbf{x})\)
. Finally we denote the differentiable finite element method (FEM) solver as
\(f\)
, which takes the density field as input and returns the structure’s compliance.  Therefore, the optimization problem can be formulated as follows:
\[
\begin{equation}
\min_{\theta} f(\rho(g(\theta))).
\end{equation}
\]
Here,
\(\theta\)
is the vector of design variables (the
\(y\)
-coordinates of the vertices).
AD and Tesseracts
¶
Since we want use a gradient based optimizer, we need to compute the gradient of the compliance with respect to the design variables. Hence we are interested in the following derivative:
\[
\begin{equation}
\frac{\partial f}{\partial\theta} = \frac{\partial f}{\partial \rho} \cdot \frac{\partial \rho}{\partial g} \cdot \frac{\partial g}{\partial\theta}
\end{equation}
\]
Note that each term is a (Jacobian) matrix. With modern AD libraries such as
JAX
, backpropagation uses the vector-Jacobian-product to pull back the gradients over the entire pipeline, without ever materializing Jacobian matrices. This is a powerful feature, but it typically requires that the entire pipeline is implemented in a single monolithic application – which can be cumbersome and error-prone, and does not scale well to large applications or compute needs.
With Tesseracts, we wrap each function in a separate module and then compose them together. To enable differentiability, we also define AD-relevant endpoints, such as the vector-Jacobian product, inside each Tesseract module (
tesseract_api.py
).
To learn more about building and running Tesseracts, please refer to the
Tesseract documentation
.
Setup
¶
Let’s install the required packages and build the two Tesseract images. Building the Tesseracts can take a few minutes as they are Docker containers with quite a few dependencies.

install -r requirements.txt -q --isolated

data.title: Yet Another Zip Trick
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 这篇文章（基于提供的标题和链接结构）似乎是一个网站的部分界面介绍。"Redeem items" 指可以兑换物品，"Profile" 指用户个人资料，"Settings" 是设置选项，"Log out" 表示登出，"Login" 表示登录。页面中还包含一个电子邮件联系方式 "contact@hexarcana.ch"。整体来看，这是HexArcana网站的用户界面概览，提供登录、个人设置、物品兑换及联系支持的功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于zip文件设计及其潜在安全风险的讨论

不同观点：
• socalgal2：认为zip文件的TOC（目录）是唯一的真实来源，设计上允许在不重写所有磁盘的情况下添加新文件。他指出，读取TOC以外的文件内容是无效的zip读取方式。这种设计允许在旧文件不被引用的情况下添加新文件，这是有意为之的。

• jonathanlydall：关注zip文件中包含PDF文件的安全风险，认为这种情况本身就很可疑。他分享了自己处理可疑邮件的经验，特别是通过拒绝外部来源的.svg文件来阻止诈骗尝试。

• wingmanjd：提出了一个问题，询问类似zip文件结构的docx文件是否会被这种技巧欺骗，暗示这种安全隐患可能影响其他文件格式。

• soupfordummies：虽然承认现实中的安全隐患令人不快，但欣赏这种技术 exploit 的巧妙性，表现出对技术本身的兴趣。

• o11c：认为这个问题早在十年前就已经为人所知，暗示这不是一个新问题，不需要特别关注或夸大。

补充讨论：
- 关于zip文件设计的讨论集中在技术实现和历史背景上，特别是为了兼容多磁盘存储的需求。
- 安全风险的讨论主要围绕zip文件中包含的可疑文件类型（如PDF和SVG），以及如何通过邮件规则来防御潜在攻击。
- 争议焦点可能在于zip文件设计的实用性和安全性之间的平衡，以及如何在现代应用中有效应对这些潜在风险。

data.title: Wind Knitting Factory
data.author: bschne
data.article_summary: "Wind Knitting Factory" 是一个安装在建筑物外墙上的风力编织机。该机器由直径超过一米的风车驱动，风力强时编织速度快，风力弱时速度慢。编织物从屋顶向下延伸，通过窗户进入室内，人们可以看见它逐渐变长。编织物会被定期“收割”并制成围巾，每条围巾都附有标签，标明由风编织的时间和日期。这一移动风力工厂展示了风能在城市环境中的生产潜力，连接了公共和私人空间。

WIND KNITTING FACTORY
‘Wind Knitting Factory’ is a wind powered knitting machine that is attached to the facade of a building. The blades embrace more than a meter in diameter, and the wind that is cached by the mill drives the machine. Like that a long scarf gets knitted along the building downward. When it is windy the machine knits fast and with less wind the machine knits slowly.
﻿From the top of the façade the knitwear drops along the front, until a window has been reached. Trough the window the knitwear gets continues transported inside, where people can see it becoming longer and longer. Occasionally the knitwear gets ‘harvested’ and transformed into scarves. Every scarf gets a label which tells you the time and the date on which the wind made the scarf.
This mobile wind factory, which operates between the public and the private space, illustrates a production process and visualizes what you can produce with the present urban wind.
