本文讨论了作者在家庭实验室重建中寻找小型NAS设备的过程，重点关注NVMe SSD存储和Intel高效芯片的结合。作者需要大约6TB的可用存储空间，并评估了三款新发布的小型NAS：GMKtec G9、Aiffro K100和Beelink ME mini。这些设备均采用Intel N100/N150芯片，支持多条PCIe通道和多个M.2 NVMe SSD插槽，同时具备2.5Gbps网络接口。

GMKtec G9价格实惠，但早期版本存在散热问题，新版有所改进。Aiffro K100体积更小、散热更好，但缺少eMMC和WiFi，且只有一个网络接口。Beelink ME mini最为安静，拥有6个NVMe插槽和内置电源，散热和性能表现良好，但价格可能较高。

每款设备都有其优缺点，选择时需根据个人需求权衡。如果空间和电源允许，也可以考虑全尺寸NAS。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：小型NAS设备及其相关技术的优缺点，包括硬件配置、散热、数据保护、功耗以及在不同使用场景下的适用性。

不同观点：
• transpute认为Intel N150的TXT/DRTM功能非常有用，尤其是在安全性要求高的场景中，如Qubes和Proxmox等系统。同时提到未配备Bootguard的N150设备可能支持coreboot，这为定制化和安全性提供了更多可能性。
• sandreas则对小型设备持保留态度，认为其在可升级性、ECC内存支持、散热和I/O方面存在不足，更倾向于使用mATX主板的解决方案。
• bee_rider提出mini-NAS可能代表了一种新的设计目标，适用于需要低功耗和较小存储空间的场景，不同于传统的大型NAS。
• dwood_dev对N100系列的低功耗x86小型PC表示赞赏，并关注具体设备的USB-C PD功能。
• Havoc分享了使用四核NVMe mini-NAS的经验，认为在无ECC内存的情况下，这些设备仍能提供不错的性能，特别是在风扇散热和RAID配置方面。
• monster_truck希望看到更强大和高端的mini-NAS，如搭载Ryzen 7745和128GB ECC DDR5内存的设备，尽管其功耗和噪音可能较高。
• koeng关注是否有支持ECC内存的mini NAS，认为这是其选择的主要限制因素。
• guerby寻找可通过USB-C供电的UPS解决方案，以确保服务器在断电时的持续运行。
• rbanffy对数据存储量提出疑问，认为大多数用户的存储需求可能在4TB左右，而非更高容量。
• herf讨论了适合NAS的SSD选择，关注PLP、写入耐久性和ZFS兼容性等问题。
• cuu508询问非Intel的低功耗mini NAS选项，提到了FriendlyElec CM3588。
• irusensei分享了使用MS-01和NVMe配置的经验，强调了TPM全盘加密和远程管理功能。
• karczex指出NAND内存的缺点，包括需要定期刷新和存储超过80%时性能下降的问题。
• noisy_boy提到在没有有线网络的环境中使用mini-NAS的挑战，主要涉及WiFi访问。
• ezschemi对比了不同设备，最终选择了Odroid H4-Ultra，并对其性能和稳定性表示满意，尽管其成本较高。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是mini NAS在可升级性、散热、ECC内存支持等方面的不足，以及这些设备是否适合不同用户的需求。
• 另一个讨论点是SSD的选择及其在PLP、写入耐久性和ZFS兼容性方面的表现，尤其是在预算有限的情况下。
• 功耗和UPS解决方案也是讨论的重要部分，特别是在小型服务器和NAS设备中如何确保持续供电和数据安全。

44465319.article_content:
Mini NASes marry NVMe to Intel's efficient chip
I'm in the process of rebuilding my homelab from the ground up, moving from a 24U full-size 4-post rack to a
mini rack
.
One of the most difficult devices to downsize (especially
economically
) is a NAS. But as my needs have changed, I'm bucking the trend of all
datahoarders
and I need
less
storage than the 120 TB (80 TB usable) I currently have.
It turns out, when you stop running an entire YouTube channel in your home (I'm in a studio now), you don't need more than a few terabytes, so my new conservative estimate is
6
terabytes of usable space. That's within the realm of NVMe SSD storage for a few hundred bucks, so that's my new target.
Three new mini NASes were released over the past year that are great candidates, and I have relationships with all three companies making them, so I am lucky to have been offered review units of each:
GMKtec G9
Aiffro K100
Beelink ME mini
I've compiled
all
my experience with the three NASes into one concise YouTube video, which I've embedded below:
However, I thought I'd at least give a few notes here for those interested in reading, not watching.
Generally, all three mini NASes use an Intel N100/N150 chip, and divvy up its 9 PCIe Gen 3 lanes into 4 (or in the Beelink's case, 6) M.2 NVMe SSD slots. They all have 2.5 Gbps networking, though the GMKtec and Beelink have
dual
2.5 Gbps NICs.
The difference is in the execution, and each box has one or two minor issues that keep me from giving a whole-hearted recommendation. When you're dealing with tiny devices, there's
always
a compromise. So you have to see which compromises you're most willing to deal with. (Or just buy a full size NAS if you have the space/power for it.)
GMKtec G9
I previously reviewed this NAS in April; see my blog post
The (almost) perfect mini NAS for my mini rack
.
That 'almost' is doing a lot of heavy lifting, though; there were inherent cooling issues if you ran the box with four NVMe drives, and it was bad enough GMKtec went through a design revision.
Their newer version of the G9 has a much larger cooling vent on the side, and I believe they may have tweaked some other aspects of the design. I'm not sure how it ends up, though, so I'll have to post an updated review if I can get my hands on one of these updated models.
Aiffro K100
The K100 is even smaller than the G9, and it keeps things cool much better, likely owing to much more ventilation on the sides, a heatsink that covers VRMs (Voltage Regulation Modules) and some of the other hot chips, and a full metal enclosure.
The major downside is despite costing $299 (over $100 more than the G9's base spec), it drops eMMC (so you have to install an OS on one of the 4 NVMe SSDs, or on an external USB stick), and drops WiFi (this is wired only—and a single 2.5 Gbps port versus 2 on the other two mini NASes.
The BIOS is also very light on customization, only really allowing tweaking the power restore behavior and performance profile.
But it's very quiet (less than 37 dBa under load), absolutely tiny, and uses the least power of all the Intel mini NASes I tested.
Beelink ME mini
Speaking of quiet, the ME mini is even more quiet. It's not
silent
, but the larger fan and 'chimney' heatsink design (reminiscent of Apple's Trash Can Mac) mean it can keep from throttling even in 'performance' mode indefinitely—and barely scratch 35 dBa while doing so.
It has not 4 but
6
NVMe slots, though 5 of those slots are PCIe Gen 3 x1 (one lane of bandwidth is 8 GT/sec), and the last slot is x2 (two lanes).
If you order one with a Crucial SSD pre-installed, it will be installed in that last x2 slot for maximum performance—and the test unit I was shipped came with Windows 11 preinstalled.
But it has built-in eMMC (64 GB), and I installed Ubuntu on that for my testing. Another nice feature is a built-in power supply, which is quite rare on these mini PCs. Often you buy the thing based on the size of the mini PC, then hanging out back, there's a DC power supply the same size as the mini PC!
Not here, it's got a small power supply tucked inside one part of the heatsink, though I'm not sure how much thermal transfer there is between the heatsink and the power supply. I didn't encounter any overheating issues, though, and even with the preinstalled Crucial SSD only touching the thermal pad where the NVMe controller chip sits (there was an air gap between the thermal pad and all the flash storage chips), I didn't have any concerns over thermals.
It did run a little hotter overall than the K100, but it was also in full performance/turbo boost mode, whereas the K100 comes from the factory with a more balanced power profile.
Conclusion
The G9 is definitely the winner in terms of price, but the cooling tradeoffs at least with the initial revision I reviewed were not worth it, because it would lock up and reboot if it overheated. The ME mini is currently $209 (starting) on pre-sale, but that price could go up:
All three NASes would perform

data.title: Nvidia won, we all lost
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: NVIDIA的RTX 50系列显卡发布后问题频出。首先，黄牛机器人抢购导致消费者难以购买，且库存不足引发饥饿营销猜测。其次，显卡的熔断电源连接问题仍未解决，设计缺陷导致连接器可能熔化。此外，部分显卡出厂时缺少处理单元（ROP），影响性能。NVIDIA的驱动程序也出现问题，消费者对性能提升不满意。相比之下，苹果在硬件发布时能保证充足库存，而NVIDIA似乎更关注数据中心GPU市场，消费级显卡逐渐边缘化。总体来看，RTX 50系列面临供应、设计和性能等多重问题，消费者购买体验不佳。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：NVIDIA的市场主导地位及其争议

不同观点：
• **NVIDIA的市场主导与消费者的困境**：一些用户认为NVIDIA在GPU市场的主导地位对消费者不利，导致价格上涨和供应短缺。Turbobrew指出，消费者在抱怨被剥削的同时，仍然继续购买，这种行为助长了市场的恶性循环。他还将这种情况与《魔法集结》(Magic: The Gathering)的消费行为相比较，认为人们在不满的同时仍然继续消费。

• **NVIDIA有意控制市场供应**：一些评论如neuroelectron和Kon5ole认为，NVIDIA可能故意保持高端GPU的低供应量，以制造高需求的假象，从而维持高价。Kon5ole进一步解释，由于AI和企业市场的需求旺盛，消费级GPU实际上是由企业级芯片的“边角料”制造的，导致供应不足。

• **NVIDIA在技术创新和市场策略上的成功**：dagaci认为NVIDIA在技术创新和市场时机把握上表现出色，成功引领了多个市场 boom。同时，他认为批评NVIDIA的人没有给予其足够的肯定，特别是在其主导的市场领域。

• **对NVIDIA产品质量和工程问题的批评**：一些用户如leakycap和rkagerer对NVIDIA产品的实际性能和工程质量提出质疑。leakycap认为NVIDIA的高端产品在性能上并没有显著提升，不值得高价升级。rkagerer则从工程角度批评NVIDIA产品的设计缺陷，特别是其可能导致火灾风险的电缆问题，并呼吁集体诉讼和产品召回。

• **对市场操控和虚假宣传的质疑**：ionwake对NVIDIA在发布会上的“舞台谎言”表示不满，特别是关于其展示的机器人是否真正具备自主能力的问题。他认为这种行为会损害公司的信誉，并引起消费者的质疑。

补充讨论：
• **市场竞争与替代选择**：一些用户如monster_truck表示，只要NVIDIA有竞争对手，他们会继续支持其他公司。如果所有公司都失败，他们会考虑自己创办公司。这显示了对NVIDIA不信任的深层次情感。

• **价格与供需关系的经济学讨论**：一些评论如strictnein和hiAndrewQuinn从经济学角度分析了NVIDIA产品的价格问题，认为NVIDIA并没有从黄牛高价销售中获益，且市场上的高价可能是因为NVIDIA的定价过低导致的供需失衡。

• **GPU市场的演变**：cherioo和snitty指出，高端GPU正逐渐从发烧友产品转变为奢侈品，中端GPU已经能满足大多数需求，这使得高端GPU的市场竞争变得不再那么激烈。

争议焦点：
• NVIDIA是否故意控制市场供应以维持高价和高需求假象。
• NVIDIA在发布会上的“舞台谎言”是否构成对消费者的误导。
• NVIDIA产品的工程质量和安全性问题是否应该引起更大的关注和法律行动。

44468175.article_content:
Since the disastrous launch of the RTX 50 series, NVIDIA has been unable to escape negative headlines: scalper bots are snatching GPUs away from consumers before official sales even begin, power connectors continue to melt, with no fix in sight, marketing is becoming increasingly deceptive, GPUs are missing processing units when they leave the factory, and the drivers, for which NVIDIA has always been praised, are currently falling apart. And to top it all off, NVIDIA is becoming increasingly insistent that media push a certain narrative when reporting on their hardware.
Whatâs an MSRP anyway?
Just like with every other GPU launch in recent memory, this one has also been ripe with scalper bots snatching up stock before any real person could get any for themselves. Retailers have reported that theyâve received
very little stock to begin with
. This in turn sparked rumors about NVIDIA purposefully keeping stock low to make it look like the cards are in high demand to drive prices. And sure enough, on secondary markets, the cards go
way above
MSRP and some retailers have started to
bundle the cards with other inventory
(PSUs, monitors, keyboards and mice, etc.) to inflate the price even further and get rid of stuff in their warehouse people wouldnât buy otherwiseâand you donât even get a working computer out of spending over twice as much as a GPU alone would cost you.
Newegg selling the ASUS ROG Astral GeForce RTX 5090 for $3,359 (MSRP: $1,999)
eBay Germany offering the same ASUS ROG Astral RTX 5090 for â¬3,349,95 (MSRP: â¬2,229)
I had a look at GPU prices for previous generation models for both AMD and NVIDIA as recently as May 2025 and I wasnât surprised to find even RTX 40 series are still very much overpriced, with the GeForce RTX 4070 (lower mid-tier) starting at $800 (MSRP: $599), whereas the same money can get you a Radeon RX 7900 XT (the second best GPU in AMDâs last generation lineup). The discrepancy in bang for buck couldnât be more jarring. And thatâs before considering that NVIDIA gave out defective chips to board partners that were
missing ROPs
(Raster Operations Pipelines) from the factory, thus reducing their performance. Or, how NVIDIA put it in a statement to
The Verge
:
We have identified a rare issue affecting less than 0.5% (half a percent) of GeForce RTX 5090 / 5090D and 5070 Ti GPUs which have one fewer ROP than specified. The average graphical performance impact is 4%, with no impact on AI and Compute workloads. Affected consumers can contact the board manufacturer for a replacement. The production anomaly has been corrected.
Those 4% can make an RTX 5070 Ti perform at the levels of an RTX 4070 Ti Super, completely eradicating the reason youâd get an RTX 5070 Ti in the first place. Not to mention that the generational performance uplift over the RTX 40 series was already received quite poorly in general. NVIDIA also had to later amend their statement to The Verge and admit the RTX 5080 was also missing ROPs.
Itâs adding insult to injury with the cardsâ general
unobtainium
and it becomes even more ridiculous when you compare NVIDIA to another trillion dollar company that is also in the business of selling hardware to consumers: Apple.
How is it that one can supply customers with enough stock on launch consistently for decades, and the other canât? The only reason I can think of is, that NVIDIA just doesnât care. Theyâre making the big bucks with data center GPUs now, selling the shovels that drive the âAIâ bullshit gold rush, to the point that selling to consumers is
increasingly becoming
a rounding error on their balance sheets.
These cards are ð¥ð¥ð¥ (and not the good kind)
The RTX 50 series are the second generation of NVIDIA cards to use the 12VHPWR connector. The RTX 40 series became infamous as the GPU series with melting power connectors. So did they fix that?
No
. The cables can still melt, both on the GPU and PSU. Itâs a design flaw in the board of the GPU itself which cannot be fixed unless the circuitry of the cards is replaced with a new design.
With the RTX 30 cards, each power input (i.e. the cables from the power supply) had its own shunt resistor
[1]
. If one pin in a power input had not been connected properly, another pin would have had to take over in its stead. If both pins were not carrying any current, there would have been no phase on the shunt resistor and the card would not have started up. Youâd get a black screen, but the hardware would still be fine.
NVIDIA, in its infinite wisdom, changed this design starting with the RTX 40 series.
Instead of individual shunt resistors for each power input, the shunt resistors are now connected in parallel to all pins of the power input from a single 12VHPWR connector. Additionally, the lines are recombined behind the resistors. • **NVIDIA在技术创新和市场策略上的成功**：dagaci认为NVIDIA在技术创新和市场时机把握上表现出色，成功引领了多个市场 boom。同时，他认为批评NVIDIA的人没有给予其足够的肯定，特别是在其主导的市场领域。

• **对NVIDIA产品质量和工程问题的批评**：一些用户如leakycap和rkagerer对NVIDIA产品的实际性能和工程质量提出质疑。leakycap认为NVIDIA的高端产品在性能上并没有显著提升，不值得高价升级。rkagerer则从工程角度批评NVIDIA产品的设计缺陷，特别是其可能导致火灾风险的电缆问题，并呼吁集体诉讼和产品召回。

• **对市场操控和虚假宣传的质疑**：ionwake对NVIDIA在发布会上的“舞台谎言”表示不满，特别是关于其展示的机器人是否真正具备自主能力的问题。他认为这种行为会损害公司的信誉，并引起消费者的质疑。

补充讨论：
• **市场竞争与替代选择**：一些用户如monster_truck表示，只要NVIDIA有竞争对手，他们会继续支持其他公司。如果所有公司都失败，他们会考虑自己创办公司。这显示了对NVIDIA不信任的深层次情感。

• **价格与供需关系的经济学讨论**：一些评论如strictnein和hiAndrewQuinn从经济学角度分析了NVIDIA产品的价格问题，认为NVIDIA并没有从黄牛高价销售中获益，且市场上的高价可能是因为NVIDIA的定价过低导致的供需失衡。

• **GPU市场的演变**：cherioo和snitty指出，高端GPU正逐渐从发烧友产品转变为奢侈品，中端GPU已经能满足大多数需求，这使得高端GPU的市场竞争变得不再那么激烈。

争议焦点：
• NVIDIA是否故意控制市场供应以维持高价和高需求假象。
• NVIDIA在发布会上的“舞台谎言”是否构成对消费者的误导。
• NVIDIA产品的工程质量和安全性问题是否应该引起更大的关注和法律行动。

data.title: The Sewing Machine's Broken
data.author: altilunium
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了作者修理坏掉的缝纫机电动机的过程。起初，他发现碳棒（carbon rod）可能导致问题，打开后一个小螺丝和碳棒因弹簧机制飞出。他最终从另一台旧缝纫机上找到替代零件，发现第二根碳棒损坏，修复后电动机恢复正常。作者好奇为何缝纫机需要两根碳棒，而他的Tamiya玩具马达不需要。经过研究，他了解到缝纫机使用的是通用电动机，需要两根碳棒作为电刷来完成电流回路，而Tamiya马达虽有小电刷，但因功率低不需要大型碳棒。最终，缝纫机修好，作者的好奇心也得到了满足。

44473049.article_content:
The sewing machine’s broken
secara.teratur
3 min read
·
Just now
--
Listen
Share
“The sewing machine’s broken. Do something already!”
Alright, alright. Let’s see what’s up.
I hit the foot pedal — the motor budges a bit, makes this huge buzzing noise, then just… stops.
“Maybe the carbon rod is the problem?”
Wait. Carbon rod? Why does it need one? Isn’t an electric motor supposed to be simple? I mean, I still remember my old
Tamiya
̶d̶y̶n̶a̶m̶o̶ from back in the day — that thing never needed a carbon rod.
Curiosity piqued, I cracked open the carbon rod cover. There’s this little screw that pushes the carbon rod in with a spring. The moment I loosened it, it shot across the room — thanks, spring mechanism. And… I lost the screw. Nice.
“That’s it. You ruined it! You definitely ruined it!”
So then I rummaged through an old, dusty, unused sewing machine — pulling parts like a mad scientist. I salvaged a screw, a carbon rod — the whole kit.
Secured. Back to the operation.
The carbon rod looked fine. Still plenty left. Not worn out yet.
“There are two carbon rods. Maybe check the other one?”
Wait, TWO?! One’s already weird. Now you’re telling me there’s another? Why does this motor need two carbon rods while my tiny
Tamiya
̶d̶y̶n̶a̶m̶o̶ didn’t need any?
Anyway. I hunted down the second carbon rod — hidden way behind the motor. Couldn’t reach it while it was still mounted, so I had to pull the whole thing out.
There it was. Gotcha. The second carbon rod was busted — the rod had popped out of its spring, so it wasn’t even touching the deeper part of the motor properly.
I clipped the spring back in place, reassembled everything, and boom — the motor ran like new.
But I couldn’t help it. I wondered, why does it need two carbon rods?
One
YouTube
deep dive later, it finally clicked:
The electric motor used in a sewing machine (right) requires at least two carbon rods, which are housed in screw-type holders (right, red circle). In the motor schematic (left), these carbon rods function as brushes that deliver electrical current to the spinning commutator.
Turns out this motor is actually a universal motor — it needs two brushes (that’s what the carbon rods really are) to complete the circuit. One brush feeds current in, the other lets it flow out — while the spinning commutator switches the direction so the rotor keeps turning smoothly.
The genius bit? They use carbon because:
It’s conductive, but not too hard, so it won’t wreck the commutator.
Its graphite structure has these layers that slide easily — friction stays low.
It can handle the heat. Graphite doesn’t melt; it sublimes at high temps.
Its slight resistance helps keep sparks under control.
And it’s chemically stable when hot.
Pretty clever. But yeah — that’s also why these rods wear out over time. The constant friction slowly sands them down. So you’ve got to replace or reload the brushes every now and then.
So, back to my Tamiya ̶d̶y̶n̶a̶m̶o̶.
Did it magically work without brushes? Nope. Turns out, it has them too — but they’re tiny. Those hobby motors (Mabuchi-type) run on low voltage and current, so they don’t need big, beefy carbon rods.
“As far as I know, Mabuchi is no longer manufacturing motors for Tamiya,”
said Laperen one year ago
. But the last time I tinkered with my Tamiya dynamo was around more than a decade ago, so back then I was probably still using a Mabuchi-type motor. (Using the term dynamo is actually a bit misleading, since it technically means an electrical generator — but back then, my kid self and all my childhood friends still called it a dynamo instead of a motor. I suspect this was due to a bit of semantic drift, because in our mother tongue, the word motor already had a very different meaning: a gasoline-powered motorcycle.)
https://www.mabuchi-motor.com/product/knowledge/structure/explanation.html#tab05
They use built-in metal brushes or tiny graphite strips, and once they wear out, you toss the motor and get a new one.
Case closed.
Sewing machine : fixed.
Missing screw : cannibalized.
My curiosity : satisfied.

data.title: Lens: Lenses, Folds and Traversals
data.author: hyperbrainer
data.article_summary: 该文章介绍了Haskell库`lens`，它提供了 lenses、folds 和 traversals 等工具，用于处理数据类型的操作。`lens` 库包含许多实用的预定义 lenses，支持自动生成 lenses 和 isomorphisms，并提供丰富的组合子来操作这些结构。用户可以轻松定义自己的 lenses 和 traversals，而无需依赖 `lens` 库。库中还包含了各种模块，支持对常见 Haskell 数据类型的操作，如数组、列表、集合、映射等。此外，文章提供了示例、视频教程和相关文档链接，帮助用户理解和使用 lenses。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Haskell中使用lens库的优缺点及相关学习资源

不同观点：
• [kccqzy] 认为应该避免使用lens库中的各种操作符（如^.、^..、^?等），因为这些操作符难以记忆且像噪声。他建议使用具名函数来替代操作符，以提高代码的可读性和可维护性。
• [moomin] 表示，如果想要理解lens，这种完全避免操作符的建议并不是合适的起点，也不适合进阶学习。
• [haskman] 推荐使用PureScript中的光学指南作为更易懂的lens入门资料，认为PureScript的实现比Haskell更清晰。
• [0_gravitas] 指出Clojure中的Specter库提供了类似Optics的功能，并建议在Clojure环境中使用该库作为替代。
• [srik] 推荐使用《Optics by Example》这本书作为学习lens的资源，认为它更具连贯性和全面性，能够节省学习时间。
• [rrgok] 质疑Haskell为何不能在语法层面提供命令式接口来进行字段的get/set操作，认为这可以简化lens的使用。
• [johnfn] 批评Haskell在处理简单赋值操作（如`foo.bar.baz = 1`）时过于复杂，支持对Haskell的lens库进行简化和优化。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Haskell中lens库的操作符是否过于复杂且难以记忆。部分用户认为这些操作符影响了代码的可读性，建议使用具名函数，而另一些用户则认为这是进阶学习的必要部分。
• 不同用户推荐了多种学习资源和替代方案，如PureScript的光学指南、Clojure的Specter库以及《Optics by Example》书籍，显示出社区中对lens学习的多种路径。
• 对Haskell语法层面的改进建议（如提供命令式接口）反映了部分用户对简化lens使用方式的期望。

This package comes "Batteries Included" with many useful lenses for the types
commonly used from the Haskell Platform, and with tools for automatically
generating lenses and isomorphisms for user-supplied data types.
The combinators in
Control.Lens
provide a highly generic toolbox for composing
families of getters, folds, isomorphisms, traversals, setters and lenses and their
indexed variants.
An overview, with a large number of examples can be found in the
README
.
An introductory video on the style of code used in this library by Simon Peyton Jones is available from
Internet Archive
.
A video on how to use lenses and how they are constructed is available on
youtube
.
Slides for that second talk can be obtained from
comonad.com
.
More information on the care and feeding of lenses, including a brief tutorial and motivation
for their types can be found on the
lens wiki
.
A small game of
pong
and other more complex examples that manage their state using lenses can be found in the
example folder
.
Lenses, Folds and Traversals
With some signatures simplified, the core of the hierarchy of lens-like constructions looks like:
(Local Copy)
You can compose any two elements of the hierarchy above using
(.)
from the
Prelude
, and you can
use any element of the hierarchy as any type it linked to above it.
The result is their lowest upper bound in the hierarchy (or an error if that bound doesn't exist).
For instance:
You can use any
Traversal
as a
Fold
or as a
Setter
.
The composition of a
Traversal
and a
Getter
yields a
Fold
.
Minimizing Dependencies
If you want to provide lenses and traversals for your own types in your own libraries, then you
can do so without incurring a dependency on this (or any other) lens package at all.
e.g.
for a data type:
data Foo a = Foo Int Int a
You can define lenses such as
-- bar :: Lens' (Foo a) Int
bar :: Functor f => (Int -> f Int) -> Foo a -> f (Foo a)
bar f (Foo a b c) = fmap (\a' -> Foo a' b c) (f a)
-- quux :: Lens (Foo a) (Foo b) a b
quux :: Functor f => (a -> f b) -> Foo a -> f (Foo b)
quux f (Foo a b c) = fmap (Foo a b) (f c)
without the need to use any type that isn't already defined in the
Prelude
.
And you can define a traversal of multiple fields with
Control.Applicative.Applicative
:
-- traverseBarAndBaz :: Traversal' (Foo a) Int
traverseBarAndBaz :: Applicative f => (Int -> f Int) -> Foo a -> f (Foo a)
traverseBarAndBaz f (Foo a b c) = Foo <$> f a <*> f b <*> pure c
What is provided in this library is a number of stock lenses and traversals for
common haskell types, a wide array of combinators for working them, and more
exotic functionality, (
e.g.
getters, setters, indexed folds, isomorphisms).

data.article_summary: 美国高官建议让H5N1禽流感病毒在养鸡场中传播，以找出具有免疫力的鸡只，但专家警告这种做法可能加速病毒向人类传播，增加新 pandemic 的风险。病毒已在多种哺乳动物中传播，虽然目前人类间传播风险低，但延长病毒存活时间会增加其突变和适应人类的机会。当前政策要求感染禽流感的商用家禽需扑杀以控制传播，而官方的激进建议引发了专家担忧。政府的五点策略包括提高农场生物安全、资助农民和疫苗研究等措施。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Kennedy提案的可行性及相关影响，特别是与H5N1感染和家禽养殖业的关系。

不同观点：
• **adriand**：质疑Kennedy提案的可行性，指出家禽养殖中的鸟类是通过不同繁殖种群产生的后代，自身并不繁殖。因此，即使有部分鸟类能在H5N1感染中存活，它们的抗病基因也无法传递给下一代，这是一个重大缺陷。

• **babymetal**：对Kennedy的书《The Real Anthony Fauci》的出版质量提出质疑，指出其装帧和过多的脚注影响了阅读体验。虽然提供了Goodreads上的评分作为参考，但本人并未阅读该书，讨论重点更多在于出版质量而非提案本身。

• **valgor**：从动物权利活动家的角度支持Kennedy的提案，认为如果家禽因感染大量死亡，鸡蛋价格上涨将有助于推动替代品的讨论和使用，如植物蛋替代品。这有助于动物权利运动，并提到JUST Egg等公司可能从中获益。

• **BLKNSLVR**：担心Kennedy提案会对美国本地鸡蛋生产业造成毁灭性打击，导致价格上涨，并与特朗普的政治目标相悖，可能需要重新振兴本地产业。

• **xracy**：讽刺Kennedy是素食者，暗示他对家禽养殖业的问题可能并不关心。

• **cjk**：对当前政府在卫生和公共服务部的任命表示不满，特别批评Kennedy被任命为该职位，认为他缺乏生物学知识且受阴谋论影响，可能对美国医疗系统造成不可挽回的损害。并怀疑Kennedy的“鸡 Eugenics”计划是否可行。

• **9283409232**：简要描述Kennedy的提案类似于“鸡的优生学”，即通过感染筛选出免疫的鸟类，以增强整体种群的抗病能力。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Kennedy提案的科学性和实际可行性，尤其是基因遗传和抗病性传递的问题。
• 不同评论者从科学、经济、政治和动物权利等多个角度对提案进行了分析和批评。
• 部分评论者对Kennedy担任卫生和公共服务部职务的能力和资格提出质疑，担心其决策可能基于错误信息。

RFK's suggestion to let the H5N1 virus spread could make spillover to humans more likely, experts warn.
(Image credit: Samuel Corum via Getty Images)
High-ranking federal officials have suggested that bird flu virus should be left to "rip" through poultry farms across the U.S. — but experts warn that this hands-off approach could hasten the beginning of a new
pandemic
Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the secretary of Health and Human Services, and
Brooke Rollins
, secretary of Agriculture, have floated the notion that instead of culling birds infected with the highly pathogenic H5N1 virus, farmers should let it spread through flocks. The idea is that by doing this, farmers can "identify the birds, and preserve the birds, that are immune to it," Kennedy
told Fox News
on March 11.
Now, a perspective piece authored by a group of virologists, veterinarians and health security experts argues that the plan would not only be ineffective, but could also increase the risk of the virus spilling over into humans and sparking a new pandemic. The researchers published their arguments July 3 in the journal
Science
.
You may like
Deadly measles outbreaks could explode across the US if vaccinations fall, model predicts
2-in-1 COVID-flu vaccine looks promising, but approval could be delayed
When will the US measles outbreak end?
"Essentially, the longer you allow a virus that has shown to be effective in infecting multiple hosts survive in an environment, the greater the chance you give it to spread, to mutate, and to try its luck at adaptation," perspective first-author
Erin Sorrell
, a virologist at the Johns Hopkins Center for Health Security, told Live Science. "Worse case scenario, the virus adapts and expands its host range to become transmissible in humans … Now we have a pandemic."
Bird flu in the U.S.
H5N1 is a subtype of highly pathogenic avian
influenza
(HPAI), a type of bird flu that can cause severe disease and death in poultry and other birds. Since the virus began spreading widely among U.S. birds in January 2022, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
has reported
that more than 174 million birds across all 50 states have been infected with the disease. The virus’s transmission among wild aquatic birds, commercial poultry and backyard, hobbyist flocks, has led to massive culls in farms and sent egg prices skyrocketing.
The virus typically transmits among wild birds and poultry, but it's known to have also infected more than
48 mammal species
, including foxes, skunks, raccoons,
seals
and
polar bears
. It has also spread to dairy cattle, causing outbreaks in more than
1,000 herds across 17 U.S. states
, according to current estimates.
Related:
How to avoid bird flu

Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.
Contact me with news and offers from other Future brands
Receive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors
Isolated human cases
have been reported
amid the ongoing outbreak in animals, primarily among farm workers, according to the CDC, although the agency states that the current health risk to the general public remains low. This is because, while the disease can spread among different animals, it currently can't be passed from human to human.
Federal plans
Rollins recently issued updates about the U.S. government's plan to combat the infection's spread and lower egg prices. The
five-pronged strategy
denotes $500 million to improve farm biosecurity, $400 million in financial aid to farmers and $100 million for vaccine research. The government is also exploring ways to slash regulations and increase temporary import options for eggs.
Current regulations state that when infections are detected among commercial poultry, farmers must cull the affected flocks to contain the disease's spread, for which they are financially compensated by the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA).
Yet suggestions made by officials for more radical ways to manage bird flu have left experts concerned. In May, Kennedy and
Dr. Mehmet Oz
, the administrator for the U.S. Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services,
voiced their support
for the owners of a Canadian ostrich farm whose 398 birds faced a cull following confirmed cases of H5N1 bird flu in December 2024 and January this year.
"We believe significant scientific knowledge may be garnered from following the ostriches in a controlled environment," Kennedy wrote in a letter
posted to the social platform X
and addressed to the head of the Canadian Food Inspection Agency, which had ordered the cull. Kennedy suggested that the ostriches may have already acquired some "downstream immunity" to the virus, and Oz offered to relocate the birds to his Florida ranch for further study.
A close-up of chickens in an industrial farm.
(Image credit: KARRASTOCK via Getty Images)

data.title: EverQuest
data.author: dmazin
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了MMORPG（大型多人在线角色扮演游戏）发展史的一部分，聚焦于《无尽的任务》（EverQuest）如何在1990年代末超越《网络创世纪》（Ultima Online）取得成功。尽管《网络创世纪》率先证明了此类游戏的市场潜力，但《无尽的任务》通过避免前者的错误，成功吸引了数十万玩家，并创造了巨大收益。文章还介绍了《无尽的任务》的诞生过程，其开发源于索尼互动美国工作室的一个内部项目，由年轻制片人约翰·斯梅德利（John Smedley）主导，尽管该项目与索尼当时的核心业务（如PlayStation的体育游戏）无关。斯梅德利受到早期网络游戏《无冬之夜》的启发，决心实现一个能让玩家在线体验《龙与地下城》式冒险的梦想，最终在老板的支持下成功推动了项目。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：EverQuest（EQ）游戏的回顾与影响，以及相关争议

不同观点：
• **开发与实验环境**：don_neufeld提到EverQuest的订阅收入为公司提供了实验温床，促成了多种MMO类型的尝试，包括未发布的MMO RTS。此外，还提及了与J.K.罗琳商讨制作哈利波特MMO但未果的经历。
• **法律争议**：0points指出Daybreak正在起诉一个受欢迎的EverQuest模拟服务器The Heroes Journey，该服务器因提供新形式的EverQuest而受到玩家欢迎。
• **怀旧与现实**：mike1o1和azretd都表达了对EverQuest的怀旧情感，但同时指出由于现实生活责任的增加，无法再像过去那样投入时间玩这种需要大量时间投入的游戏。
• **独特游戏体验**：j_timberlake分享了一个因游戏中的声望系统而导致角色被NPC守卫攻击的独特经历，认为这种设计在其他游戏中很少见。
• **游戏对个人发展的影响**：peripitea和daeken强调EverQuest不仅是一个游戏，更是他们职业生涯的重要起点，通过游戏中的策略研究和管理技能，以及技术学习，为他们后来的职业发展奠定了基础。

补充讨论：
• **游戏成瘾问题**：lordnacho和tmountain分享了关于EverQuest成瘾的个人见闻，描述了因过度沉迷游戏而影响学业和工作的真实案例。
• **技术与文化讨论**：numinix和michaelcampbell针对EverQuest的图像和模型进行了技术性讨论，包括对游戏中“goblin butt”模型的对比和确认。
• **社区与文化影响**：rudimentary_phy提到EverQuest提升了他的打字技能，而thom则通过链接分享了一个EverQuest粉丝文化的页面，强调了EverQuest在社区中的持久影响。

争议焦点：
• **法律争议**：Daybreak对EverQuest模拟服务器的诉讼是当前讨论中的一个主要争议点，涉及到版权、玩家社区以及游戏公司之间的关系。
• **游戏成瘾与责任**：玩家社区中对于EverQuest成瘾问题的讨论，涉及到游戏成瘾对个人生活的影响以及游戏公司在此方面的责任。

总的来说，评论主要围绕EverQuest的开发历史、玩家体验、技术细节、成瘾问题以及法律争议展开，展示了这款游戏在多个层面的深远影响。

The Digital Antiquarian
A history of computer entertainment and digital culture by Jimmy Maher
Home
About Me
Ebooks
Hall of Fame
Table of Contents

This Week on The Analog Antiquarian
EverQuest
04
Jul
This article tells part of the story of
MMORPGs
.
It isn’t always or even usually the pioneers who reap the rewards of the trails they blaze. As often as not, some pragmatic Johnny-come-lately pops in to make off with the booty.
Such was the case in the MMORPG space in the late 1990s. There
Ultima Online
demonstrated that there was an audience for a persistent fantasy world where people could live out alternative existences together through the magic of the Internet. Yet it was another game called
EverQuest
that turned the proof of concept into a thriving business that enthralled hundreds of thousands of players for years on end, generating enormous amounts of money in the process. For, while the first-mover advantage should not be underestimated, there’s something to be said for being the second mover as well.
EverQuest
got to watch from backstage as
Ultima Online
flubbed line after line and stumbled over assorted pieces of scenery. Then, with a list in hand of what
not
to do, it was able to stride confidently onto center stage to a standing ovation. No one ever said that show business is fair.
EverQuest
came to evince a markedly different personality than
Ultima Online
, but its origin story bears some uncanny similarities to that of the older rival it demolished. Like
Ultima Online
,
EverQuest
was born as a sort of skunk-works project within a larger company whose upper management really wasn’t all that interested in it. Like
Ultima Online
,
EverQuest
enjoyed the support of just one executive within said company, who set it in motion and then protected and nourished it like the proverbial mother hen. And like the executive behind
Ultima Online
, the one behind
EverQuest
plucked a pair of designers out of utter obscurity to help him hatch the egg.
Perhaps the most surprising aspect of the
EverQuest
origin story is the name of the company where it all went down: Sony Interactive Studios America. Suffice to say that, if you were to guess circa 1996 which publisher and studio would launch a market-transforming MMORPG later in the decade, Sony would not be high in your rankings. The Japanese mega-corp was flying high at the time, with a prominent footprint in most sectors of home electronics and mainstream entertainment, but it had hardly any presence at all on personal computers. The
Sony PlayStation
, launched in September of 1995 in North America and Europe, was on its way to becoming the most successful single games console of the twentieth century, a true mass-market cultural sensation that broadened the demographic for videogames and forever changed the way that the public perceived them. With a mainstream pile driver like that to hand, why should Sony want to waste its time with a wonky virtual world for nerds cosplaying as dwarves and mages?
It wound up doing so thanks to one man. At the beginning of 1996, John Smedley had been working for a few years as a producer at Sony Interactive, which focused almost exclusively on sports games for the PlayStation. Just 28 years old, Smedley already had a corner office with a view and a salary to match, as he and his colleagues rode the wave of the console’s incredible early success.
There was just one problem: Smedley didn’t particularly like sports, whether they happened to be played on the field or on the television screen. He had grown up as one of the kids that the jocks made fun of, the kind who walked to school every day with a
Dungeons & Dragons
rule book or two under his arm. It was only thanks to opportunism and happenstance that he had wound up helming projects aimed at gamers who worshiped John Madden rather than Gary Gygax. Now, he thought that the burgeoning Internet would soon make it possible to realize an old dream of 1980s nerds like him: that of playing
Dungeons & Dragons
online, whenever it suited you, instead of only when you could arrange to meet in person with five or so like-minded friends — assuming you even had such friends. He had a rough blueprint for how it might work, in the form of
Neverwinter Nights
, a
game on America Online
that let you effectively play one of the old single-player
SSI Gold Box CRPGS
over the Internet, taking a persistent character through a series of adventures with friends and strangers. It was limited in a thousand ways, but it was, so Smedley believed, the harbinger of a whole new category of game. And, after working for so long on games he really didn’t care about, he wanted to make one that he could feel passionate about.
Smedley took his idea to his boss Kelly Flock, the newly arrived head of Sony Interactive. It was a crazy thing to propose on the face of it, having absolutely nothing to do with anything the studio had ever done before nor any of the strategic priorities of the mother corporation; the

data.author: bnkty
data.article_summary: BunkerWeb是一款开源的下一代Web应用防火墙（WAF），基于NGINX，旨在使web服务默认安全。它可以无缝集成到Linux、Docker、Swarm、Kubernetes等环境，作为反向代理使用，并提供可配置的安全功能和便捷的网页用户界面（UI），避免了命令行操作的麻烦。BunkerWeb包含核心安全功能，并通过插件系统扩展额外功能。其特点包括HTTPS支持与Let's Encrypt自动化、先进的web安全措施、集成ModSecurity WAF及OWASP核心规则集、自动禁止可疑行为、限制连接和请求、阻止恶意机器人及已知的恶意IP等。此外，BunkerWeb提供专业服务支持，并可通过BunkerWeb Cloud实现全托管服务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：BunkerWeb及其PRO版本的特性、价格、实用性以及与其他类似工具（如OWASP ModSecurity、Caddy、Nginx Proxy Manager等）的比较。

不同观点：
• chrismorgan认为BunkerWeb PRO的介绍过于模糊，没有清晰说明与开源版本的具体区别，只提到“满足专业需求的额外功能和服务”，但未具体列举。
• stevenicr提到BunkerWeb看起来很有用，尤其是应对自动化攻击和机器人流量。但他对BunkerWeb PRO的高昂年费（1500美元/年）表示质疑，认为定价和目标用户不明确。
• jnettome对BunkerWeb给予积极评价，尤其是在使用Docker Swarm自托管产品时，认为其配置选项丰富，特别是在应对WAF和大量机器人流量方面表现突出。不过，他提到在切换到Kubernetes后还没有进一步使用或评估。
• seymon质疑使用BunkerWeb相比于使用OWASP ModSecurity的优势，指出ModSecurity也可以作为带有Nginx的反向代理容器使用。
• jqpabc123将BunkerWeb与Caddy进行比较，询问BunkerWeb有何优势。
• qmarchi认为BunkerWeb解决了一部分安全问题，但在当前大规模DDoS攻击频发的背景下，许多安全产品通过anycast IP范围解决问题，对BunkerWeb的独特性持保留态度。
• AgentMatrixAI关注BunkerWeb与Cloudflare的比较，尤其是其WAF功能和Cloudflare隧道的替代能力。
• dontTREATonme询问BunkerWeb与Nginx Proxy Manager是否有显著区别。
• SbEpUBz2以幽默的方式提到自己无法从BunkerWeb的演示中解禁自己，暗示可能存在用户操作方面的问题。
• sreekanth850将BunkerWeb与Safeline进行比较，询问两者的优劣。
• noobcoder关注BunkerWeb的语法是否与Nginx相同。
• lta对WAF的功能表示怀疑，认为很多WAF产品可能只是为了满足基于表格工作的安全项目，缺乏实际防护效果，希望有安全背景的人士解答。

补充讨论：
• BunkerWeb PRO的价格和具体功能不透明，导致部分用户困惑和犹豫。
• 用户对BunkerWeb与其他类似工具（如ModSecurity、Caddy、Nginx Proxy Manager等）的比较和选择存在疑问。
• 对WAF功能的实际效果存在怀疑，部分用户对其价值和必要性持保留态度。

Introduction
Overview
Make your web services secure by default!
BunkerWeb is a next-generation, open-source Web Application Firewall (WAF).
As a full-featured web server (based on
NGINX
under the hood), it protects your web services to make them "secure by default." BunkerWeb integrates seamlessly into your existing environments (
Linux
,
Docker
,
Swarm
,
Kubernetes
, …) as a reverse proxy and is fully configurable (don't panic, there is an
awesome web UI
if you don't like the CLI) to meet your specific use cases. In other words, cybersecurity is no longer a hassle.
BunkerWeb includes primary
security features
as part of the core but can be easily extended with additional ones thanks to a
plugin system
.
Why BunkerWeb?
Easy integration into existing environments
: Seamlessly integrate BunkerWeb into various environments such as Linux, Docker, Swarm, Kubernetes, and more. Enjoy a smooth transition and hassle-free implementation.
Highly customizable
: Tailor BunkerWeb to your specific requirements with ease. Enable, disable, and configure features effortlessly, allowing you to customize the security settings according to your unique use case.
Secure by default
: BunkerWeb provides out-of-the-box, hassle-free minimal security for your web services. Experience peace of mind and enhanced protection right from the start.
Awesome web UI
: Take control of BunkerWeb more efficiently with the exceptional web user interface (UI). Navigate settings and configurations effortlessly through a user-friendly graphical interface, eliminating the need for the command-line interface (CLI).
Plugin system
: Extend the capabilities of BunkerWeb to meet your own use cases. Seamlessly integrate additional security measures and customize the functionality of BunkerWeb according to your specific requirements.
Free as in "freedom"
: BunkerWeb is licensed under the free
AGPLv3 license
, embracing the principles of freedom and openness. Enjoy the freedom to use, modify, and distribute the software, backed by a supportive community.
Professional services
: Get technical support, tailored consulting, and custom development directly from the maintainers of BunkerWeb. Visit the
BunkerWeb Panel
for more information.
Security features
Explore the impressive array of security features offered by BunkerWeb. While not exhaustive, here are some notable highlights:
HTTPS
support with transparent
Let's Encrypt
automation: Easily secure your web services with automated Let's Encrypt integration, ensuring encrypted communication between clients and your server.
State-of-the-art web security
: Benefit from cutting-edge web security measures, including comprehensive HTTP security headers, prevention of data leaks, and TLS hardening techniques.
Integrated
ModSecurity WAF
with the
OWASP Core Rule Set
: Enjoy enhanced protection against web application attacks with the integration of ModSecurity, fortified by the renowned OWASP Core Rule Set.
Automatic ban
of strange behaviors based on HTTP status codes: BunkerWeb intelligently identifies and blocks suspicious activities by automatically banning behaviors that trigger abnormal HTTP status codes.
Apply
connection and request limits
for clients: Set limits on the number of connections and requests from clients, preventing resource exhaustion and ensuring fair usage of server resources.
Block bots
with
challenge-based verification
: Keep malicious bots at bay by challenging them to solve puzzles such as cookies, JavaScript tests, captchas, hCaptcha, reCAPTCHA, or Turnstile, effectively blocking unauthorized access.
Block known bad IPs
with external blacklists and DNSBL: Utilize external blacklists and DNS-based blackhole lists (DNSBL) to proactively block known malicious IP addresses, bolstering your defense against potential threats.
And much more...
: BunkerWeb is packed with a plethora of additional security features that go beyond this list, providing you with comprehensive protection and peace of mind.
To delve deeper into the core security features, we invite you to explore the
security tuning
section of the documentation. Discover how BunkerWeb empowers you to fine-tune and optimize security measures according to your specific needs.
Demo
A demo website protected with BunkerWeb is available at
demo.bunkerweb.io
. Feel free to visit it and perform some security tests.
Web UI
BunkerWeb offers an optional
user interface
to manage your instances and their configurations. An online read-only demo is available at
demo-ui.bunkerweb.io
. Feel free to test it yourself.
BunkerWeb Cloud
BunkerWeb Cloud
Don't want to self-host and manage your own BunkerWeb instance(s)? You might be interested in BunkerWeb Cloud, our fully managed SaaS offering for BunkerWeb.
Try our
BunkerWeb Cloud offer
and get access to:
A fully managed BunkerWeb instance hosted in our cloud
All BunkerWeb features, including PRO ones
A monitoring platform with dashboards and alerts
Technical support to assist you with configuration

data.title: Rust and WASM for Form Validation
data.author: slau
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了使用Rust和WebAssembly（WASM）进行表单验证的简化方法。过去，使用Rust生成WASM需要复杂的工具链，如Node和Webpack，但现在过程变得更加简化。作者演示了如何创建一个包含Rust web服务器和WASM组件的项目，其中WASM组件用于表单验证。

项目结构包括一个服务器目录和一个WASM目录。首先，需要安装WASM目标并配置`wasm-pack`。然后，通过编辑`Cargo.toml`文件添加必要的依赖和库类型。使用`wasm-pack build --target web`命令生成WASM库。

服务器端使用Rocket框架来处理请求，并渲染包含表单的HTML模板。通过Rust函数验证表单提交的密码是否正确，并返回相应的模板。

整个过程展示了如何在无需复杂前端知识的情况下，利用Rust和WASM实现后端风格的Web开发。这种方法允许在前后端共享相同的代码和数据结构。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust与WebAssembly（WASM）在Web开发中的应用及其优劣

不同观点：
• **zoechi**：认为Dioxus 0.7提供的组件简化了与JavaScript的交互，前景看好，但指出WASM模块的模块化和懒加载是当前的不足，以减少初始下载大小。

• **wasmperson**：
  - 对代码中大量使用`unwrap`表示担忧，认为在某些情况下程序崩溃是不可避免的。
  - 提出WebAssembly最佳实践应包括：主要使用JavaScript处理DOM和Web API，WASM二进制文件应具有窄接口和少量函数，避免依赖第三方包或标准库，并广泛使用可变的“全局”变量。
  - 认为Rust与wasm-bindgen、web-sys的组合策略与上述最佳实践相悖，除非目标是完全避免编写JavaScript。

• **neoneye2**：分享了自己使用Rust代码同时处理前端和后端的经验，并提供了项目示例和实现链接，展示Rust在全栈开发中的实际应用。

• **reactordev**：强烈反对使用WASM处理诸如表单验证等简单任务，认为这是“用炸弹杀苍蝇”，主张WASM应仅用于IPC、Canvas、WebGPU等复杂任务，而非简单的DOM操作。

• **jedisct1**：简短地指出学习JavaScript是更好的选择。

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：使用Rust和WebAssembly进行Web开发的合理性与实用性，特别是在处理DOM交互和简单任务时的效率和必要性。
- **技术实现**：讨论了Rust与WebAssembly结合时的技术细节，如错误处理、模块化以及如何有效利用全局变量。
- **实际应用**：展示了全栈Rust项目实例，提供了对Rust和WebAssembly结合使用的实际效果的参考。

总体来看，讨论围绕着Rust与WebAssembly在Web开发中的应用价值、技术实现细节以及与JavaScript的角色分工展开。

44463916.article_content:
Rust and WASM for form validation
Sebastian Lauwers
24th Apr 2025
•
10 min read
•
Tags:
rust
,
wasm
,
programming
,
tech
For a very long time, the Rust WASM story wasn't entirely clear to me. In order to use WASM from Rust you had to use Node, Webpack, and all that jazz. This always turned me off using WebAssembly because it felt too heavy of a toolchain to get going. These days, things are much, much better.
In recent years, Rust and WebAssembly have become much more usable for pure backend-style engineers. When I say “pure backend-style”, I mean people who never wrapped their heads around React, SPAs, and all that stuff. This, unsurprisingly, includes me.
For a very long time, in order to use WASM you were strongly guided towards using Webpack and a whole array of Node-related tools in order to just get started. These days, luckily, the story has become much more streamlined. In today’s tutorial, we’re going to create a quick project which includes both a web server in Rust which renders HTML templates, and a small WASM component (served by the same web server) that does form validation.
Why?
Well, I want to keep a reference handy about how this can be done. But I also want to hear if I’m doing something wrong or suboptimally.
As to why Rust/WASM instead of standard JS or TS? For one, I like to see how far we’ve come with WASM, and there is something very appealing about having the same code shared across the frontend and the backend, especially if it means potentially having the same data structures when serialising/deserialising data from one end to the other.
I’m using form validation as a placeholder. It shows all the crucial aspects to use WASM instead of JS, like wiring up DOM events to Rust functions, and then reacting to those events.
Stack
This post is being written in early-to-mid 2025. And the stack I currently jive with is as follows:
wasm-bindgen 0.2
wasm-pack 0.13
web-sys 0.3
rocket 0.5
I’m not going to do any database-related things or anything, which allows us to keep the dependencies pretty short and sweet. Most of these are library dependencies, however
wasm-pack
is a binary that actually modifies files and prepares them for distribution. This needs to be installed locally:
#
binstall can also be used here
cargo
install wasm-pack
Project structure
Let’s create a directory structure that allows this whole setup to work. One typical approach for this is to have separate crates for the server part, and the actual wasm component. Something like this:
tutorial
├── server
└── wasm
If you want to create things quickly:
mkdir
tutorial
&&
cd
tutorial
cargo
new
--
lib
wasm
cargo
new server
If you prefer to see the entire repo instead of creating all the files yourself, there is full repository available
here
.
WASM setup
Installing wasm as a target
One thing that you might have to do is to get the compiler support to actually produce wasm binaries. Provided you use
rustup
(and you really ought to be using it), this is as simple as:
rustup
target add wasm32-unknown-unknown
You can check which targets you currently have installed with
rustup target list --installed
.
Configuring the wasm crate
Edit
Cargo.toml
and add the following section. This tells the compiler to produce a dynamic library that has a relatively stable ABI. This is similar to building a library for C/C++ interop.
[
lib
]
crate-type
=
[
"
cdylib
"
]
Let’s also pull in some dependencies while we’re editing that file:
[
dependencies
]
wasm-bindgen
=
"
0.2
"
[
dependencies
.
web-sys
]
version
=
"
0.3

features
=
[
"
Document

,
"
HtmlFormElement
"
,

HtmlInputElement
"
,

Window

,
"
console

,

Event
"
,
]
At this point, you should be able to build the library in wasm form using the following command:
wasm-pack
build
--
target
web
This will produce a few files in
pkg/
:
$
ls pkg/
package.json
wasm_bg.wasm      wasm_bg.wasm.d.ts
wasm.d.ts
wasm.js
Great, now that we’re producing a WASM library that can be loaded from a browser, it’s time to build the server.
Server side implementation
Let’s add a few libraries to our server’s
Cargo.toml
:
[
dependencies
]
rocket
=

• tasty_freeze认为，管理层对10倍生产力提升的期望过高。即使编码速度加快，总体生产力提升只有10-15%。Amdahl's law和非编码工作（如思考和沟通）限制了总体生产力的大幅提升。
• hotpotat分享了自己使用LLM（如Cursor和Claude）的成功经验，认为这些工具极大地提高了他的生产力（至少3倍），并使他能够更专注于架构和管理角色。
• martinald指出，LLM在处理Excel和CRM等数据密集型任务中具有巨大潜力，特别是在服务行业中，能够替代人类进行简单的数据转录和处理工作。
• labrador从退休程序员的角度出发，表示对LLM在关键任务中的可靠性持怀疑态度，但认可LLM在头脑风暴和研究等非编码任务中的价值。
• standardUser认为，许多对LLM的批评可能源于不正确的使用方式，自己每天使用LLM解决问题，成功率高达90%，并认为这些工具在小而实用的场景中非常有效。
• AbrahamParangi反驳了对LLM的过度批评，认为尽管存在 imprecision，过去五年中LLM在翻译、转录和代码生成等领域解决了 previously intractable 的问题。
• surglymop对AGI（通用人工智能）术语的使用感到困惑，认为缺乏明确的定义使得讨论变得模糊，并希望能有更严谨的理论框架来定义AGI。
• kgeist分享了自己公司使用LLM转录客户电话的成功案例，认为LLM在自然语言处理方面非常有用，尽管存在过度炒作，但其实际价值不容忽视。
• djoldman引用了一些知名技术专家的观点，认为GenAI对相当多的人具有显著的帮助，即使具体提升幅度因人而异。
• alganet担心LLM技术的广泛误用和投资浪费问题，认为这种趋势难以逆转，公司已经全力投入。
• jjtheblunt引用Clarke's third law，认为足够先进的技术难以与魔法区分，暗示LLM技术的先进性。
• dcre提到LLM帮助的系统性和研究性问题，反对将LLM的作用简单地贬低为无用。
• cedws指出LLM的两个基本限制：上下文大小和提示注入问题，认为这些限制在实际应用中可能导致严重问题，但常常被忽视。
• ibaikov将LLM与加密货币和NFT的炒作进行对比，认为人们往往只关注新技术的表面 hype，而忽视其复杂性和潜在发展。
• orbital-decay讨论了LLM的非确定性问题，认为现代LLM的非确定性远小于人们想象，且其准确性在需要一致结果的情况下表现良好。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及LLM的实际应用场景，如代码生成、数据转录和自然语言处理等，强调了其在不同领域的不同效用。
• 对LLM的过度炒作和实际效果之间的差距进行了反思，指出需要更理性和系统的评估。
• 讨论了LLM的技术局限性和潜在风险，如提示注入和上下文限制，这些问题在实际应用中可能导致严重后果。
• 对AGI定义的讨论反映了对新兴技术术语和概念的理论需求，以及在技术讨论中严谨定义的重要性。

data.author: dontTREATonme
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要列出了几类内容板块。首先是"feature articles"（专题文章），通常是深入探讨特定主题的文章。其次是"codesod"，可能包含与编程或代码相关的内容。接下来是"error'd"，通常涉及错误或故障的讨论和解决方案。然后是"forums"（论坛），指用户交流和讨论的社区板块。此外还有"other articles"（其他文章），涵盖不属于上述分类的其他内容。最后是"random article"（随机文章），用户可以随机浏览不同主题的文章。文章整体为网站内容的导航或介绍。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软件项目外包、技术维护中的错误处理方式及相关争议

不同观点：
• donatj认为外包团队没有遵循指示，擅自使用新的框架，并通过一个巨大的、不稳定的适配层来翻译框架，导致原有系统被破坏。他们原本只需要简单的维护，结果却得到了一个混乱的代码库，最终不得不自己修复问题，并解雇了外包团队。

• delifue将此问题归结为没有从根本原因上解决问题，而是采用外部验证的方式，类似于其他技术领域中的常见问题（如SQL注入和Windows权限管理问题）。他强调通过正确的方法（如使用预处理语句防止SQL注入）从根本上解决问题的重要性。

• nine_k用一个俄罗斯谚语表达了便宜无好货的观点，暗示低成本的外包项目可能最终会付出更高的代价。

• kgeist补充说，这种情况很常见，尤其是在安全问题上，一些网站依赖第三方安全插件而不是从根本上解决问题，如SQL注入。

• adxl和userbinator的评论带有调侃性质，adxl提到"所有的注入都属于我们"，而userbinator则提到经典的"clbuttic"错误，意指在文本替换中产生的错误。

• AdieuToLogic通过引用xkcd漫画中的"Bobby Tables"来调侃SQL注入问题。

• mjcohen的评论与主帖无关，分享了一首关于电影《盗梦空间》的诗，探讨了电影中梦境层次的速度问题。

补充讨论：
- 外包项目中的沟通和执行问题：donatj的经历显示了在技术项目外包中，明确沟通和严格执行指示的重要性，否则可能导致严重后果。
- 技术维护中的根本问题解决：delifue强调了从根本上解决问题的重要性，而不是依赖表面上的修补措施。
- 成本与质量的关系：nine_k的观点提醒了在选择外包服务时，低成本可能意味着高风险。
- 安全问题的常见性：kgeist指出在实际中，许多网站仍存在SQL注入问题，并依赖不完善的解决方案。

data.title: Serving 200M requests per day with a CGI-bin
data.author: mustache_kimono
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了使用90年代的CGI技术在现代处理高流量请求的可行性。作者回忆自己1990年代末使用CGI进行网页开发的经历，并指出CGI每次请求都启动和终止进程的方式曾被认为效率低下，因此出现了PHP和FastCGI等技术。然而，随着硬件性能的提升，使用Go和Rust等现代语言可以显著提升CGI效率。实验显示，在AMD 3700X的16线程处理器上，CGI程序每秒可处理2400多个请求，每日可达2亿次。CGI因其独立进程特性，能有效利用多核CPU。作者认为，或许应该重新采用类似1998年的方式开发网页应用，但需结合现代语言如Go和Rust。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：CGI技术的优缺点以及其在现代开发中的适用性

不同观点：
• **Kragen**：认为即使在Python中，CGI的速度也足够快，特别是在高流量网站中，CGI的启动时间并不是瓶颈。然而，他对Python标准库移除cgi模块表示不满，并考虑转向JS或Lua。

• **Reidrac**：指出如果CGI需要访问数据库，每次进程启动时都需要打开连接。使用如FastCGI的模型不仅可以避免启动时间惩罚，还可以实现数据库连接池或持久连接。

• **Tractor8626**：对每秒2400次请求的性能表示质疑，认为这是在牺牲性能，而且代码并没有因此变得更简单。

• **Gvalkov**：在工作中仍然使用CGI目录，认为只要保持简单，CGI的使用体验很好。他介绍了使用uwsgi和其CGI插件来实现更好的灵活性和安全性。

• **Faizshah**：认为CGI在快速原型设计和允许客户扩展本地软件方面有优势，特别是与FastCGI模型结合使用时。

• **Indigodaddy**：提到旧的PHP脚本如CuteNews和sNews，暗示CGI技术在过去有其应用场景。

• **Jarofgreen**：讨论了Apache的.htaccess功能，虽然性能略差，但在现代硬件条件下可以接受。

• **Johnisgood**：回忆过去用C程序和CGI的经历，认为在现代硬件条件下CGI更加可行。

• **Petesergeant**：指出mod_php相对于mod_perl的设计选择使得PHP脚本运行更快，并分享了关于CGI历史的演示文稿。

• **Ivovk**：认为连接外部资源（如数据库或HTTP客户端）时，CGI表现不佳，因为需要维护连接池以避免昂贵的初始连接阶段。

• **Slashdave**：不记得CGI是因为性能问题被淘汰，反而记得是因为安全问题。

• **Aaronblohowiak**：认为fork()在过去30年变得更便宜，CGI模型在不需要为SSL或TCP连接支付代价时工作良好，但由于语言和供应商锁定问题，CGI未成为主流。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了多种技术对比，如CGI与FastCGI、PHP与Perl等，反映了不同技术在历史发展中的演变和选择原因。
• 对于CGI的性能问题，存在不同的看法，有人认为在现代硬件条件下这不是问题，而其他人则认为外部资源的连接是CGI的瓶颈。
• 也有对Python标准库变化的不满以及对旧技术 nostalgic 的回忆。

44476716.article_content:
Simon Willison’s Weblog
Subscribe
Serving 200 million requests per day with a cgi-bin
(
via
) Jake Gold tests how well 90s-era CGI works today, using a Go + SQLite CGI program running on a 16-thread AMD 3700X.
Using CGI on modest hardware, it’s possible to serve 2400+ requests per second or 200M+ requests per day.
I got my start in web development with CGI back in the late 1990s - I was a huge fan of
NewsPro
, which was effectively a weblog system before anyone knew what a weblog was.
CGI works by starting, executing and terminating a process for every incoming request. The nascent web community quickly learned that this was a bad idea, and invented technologies like PHP and
FastCGI
to help avoid that extra overhead and keep code resident in-memory instead.
This lesson ended up baked into my brain, and I spent the next twenty years convinced that you should
never
execute a full process as part of serving a web page.
Of course, computers in those two decades got a
lot
faster. I finally overcame that twenty-year core belief in 2020, when
I built datasette-ripgrep
, a Datasette plugin that shells out to the lightning fast
ripgrep
CLI tool (written in Rust) to execute searches. It worked great!
As was
pointed out on Hacker News
, part of CGI's problem back then was that we were writing web scripts in languages like Perl, Python and Java which had not been designed for lightning fast startup speeds. Using Go and Rust today helps make CGI-style requests a whole lot more effective.
Jake notes that CGI-style request handling is actually a great way to take advantage of multiple CPU cores:
These days, we have servers with 384 CPU threads. Even a small VM can have 16 CPUs. The CPUs and memory are much faster as well.
Most importantly, CGI programs, because they run as separate processes, are excellent at taking advantage of many CPUs!
Maybe we should start coding web applications like it's 1998, albeit with Go and Rust!

• **Gvalkov**：在工作中仍然使用CGI目录，认为只要保持简单，CGI的使用体验很好。他介绍了使用uwsgi和其CGI插件来实现更好的灵活性和安全性。

• **Faizshah**：认为CGI在快速原型设计和允许客户扩展本地软件方面有优势，特别是与FastCGI模型结合使用时。

• **Indigodaddy**：提到旧的PHP脚本如CuteNews和sNews，暗示CGI技术在过去有其应用场景。

• **Jarofgreen**：讨论了Apache的.htaccess功能，虽然性能略差，但在现代硬件条件下可以接受。

• **Johnisgood**：回忆过去用C程序和CGI的经历，认为在现代硬件条件下CGI更加可行。

• **Petesergeant**：指出mod_php相对于mod_perl的设计选择使得PHP脚本运行更快，并分享了关于CGI历史的演示文稿。

• **Ivovk**：认为连接外部资源（如数据库或HTTP客户端）时，CGI表现不佳，因为需要维护连接池以避免昂贵的初始连接阶段。

• **Slashdave**：不记得CGI是因为性能问题被淘汰，反而记得是因为安全问题。

• **Aaronblohowiak**：认为fork()在过去30年变得更便宜，CGI模型在不需要为SSL或TCP连接支付代价时工作良好，但由于语言和供应商锁定问题，CGI未成为主流。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了多种技术对比，如CGI与FastCGI、PHP与Perl等，反映了不同技术在历史发展中的演变和选择原因。
• 对于CGI的性能问题，存在不同的看法，有人认为在现代硬件条件下这不是问题，而其他人则认为外部资源的连接是CGI的瓶颈。
• 也有对Python标准库变化的不满以及对旧技术 nostalgic 的回忆。

data.title: On latency, measurement, and optimization in algorithmic trading systems
data.author: auc
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了算法交易系统中延迟的测量和优化挑战。在高频交易中，速度至关重要，工程师们竭尽全力优化代码和网络路径以减少执行时间。然而，测量程序的速度和实际延迟非常复杂，因为需要考虑多个层次的因素，甚至测量本身也会增加程序的开销，影响准确性。

文章通过Python伪代码示例，说明如何测量交易策略的延迟，从计算模型估值到发送订单的各个步骤。初步方法包括在关键函数周围添加计时器，但这种方法存在缺陷，比如未包含发送订单的时间、观测所有市场交易而非仅触发订单的交易等。此外，使用`datetime.now()`作为计时函数本身较慢，可能影响程序性能。改进方法是使用更精确的计时器如`time.perf_counter_ns()`，但仍未涵盖网络I/O等关键路径元素。

最终，文章强调要全面理解交易系统的延迟，必须追踪从网络数据包接收到订单发送的整个过程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何在算法交易和高性能代码中进行有效的性能测量，以及测量对代码优化的影响

不同观点：
• foobar10000：强调在交易系统中需要对各种时间粒度（如天、分钟、秒、毫秒等）进行详细的性能测量，包括软件和硬件的时间戳，以及网络卡的时间戳，以确保精确的时序相关性和延迟测量。

• tombert：通过个人经历说明异步代码的性能测量具有挑战性，因为结果可能受到调度器影响，而非代码本身的性能。这表明微基准测试可能会产生误导，需要谨慎对待。

• weinzierl：认为代码性能测量是编写高速代码的前提，但也是困难的。单次测量不可靠，建议多次测量，并指出平均值在偏斜分布中的局限性，推荐使用最小值进行比较。

• am17an：提出不仅要测量发送订单的时延，还要测量决策计算的时延，强调L1/L2交换机时间戳在端到端延迟测量中的作用，并认为创建正确的测试环境是关键。

• omgtehlion：认为在高频交易（HFT）环境中，测量相对简单，可以通过监听网络光纤进行，且这种测量不会影响延迟，甚至可以在生产环境中执行。

• nine_k：指出编写高速代码困难，但容易编写出慢速代码，因此持续测量和性能监控非常重要，建议在CI/CD流程中加入性能测试以捕获回归问题。

• Attummm：认为文章标题是点击诱饵，文章实际内容强调了编写快速算法交易系统代码和正确测量其性能的难度，呼应了其他评论者的观点。

• iammabd：认为大多数开发者只关注理想情况下的代码表现，而忽视在压力条件下的运行行为，强调了对代码性能进行全面考量的重要性。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于测量本身的复杂性和如何有效进行测量，包括对平均值和最小值在性能比较中的适用性。
- 另一个值得注意的点是不同环境（如异步代码、HFT环境）下的测量方法和其特有的挑战。
- 强调了多次测量和统计分析在代码性能评估中的重要性，以及创建可靠测试环境和工具的必要性。

How fast is it really? On latency, measurement, and optimization in algorithmic trading systems
byÂ
Brett Harrison
Blog
"The speed of light sucks." - John Carmack
â
Software engineers within the world of low-latency automated trading (colloquially known as "high-frequency trading" or HFT) obsess over speed. From purchasing private bandwidth between microwave towers to analyzing x86 instructions from different compiler versions, those with experience in this industry have seen colossal time and expense committed to the problem of optimizing code and network paths for minimal execution times.
But how does one actually measure how fast a program is? To the uninitiated, it sounds like a simple task. However, there are many layers of complexity in measuring the true latency of a trading system, or even defining what to measure in the first place. Understanding latencies in algorithmic trading systems can present Heisenberg-esque dilemmas, where the more code you write to measure latency the more overhead you add to your program and therefore the more inaccurate your measurements become.
At Architect we have been using a combination techniques to measure the latency of various codepaths and processes that comprise our institutional trading technology suite. Let's explore some solutions to these problems.
--
Let's say you've written an algorithmic trading strategy. Your strategy reacts to market trades in an instrument, perhaps by computing a proprietary model valuation, and sends an order in that instrument provided certain conditions are met. You would like to measure the time that this reaction takes
in a reproducible way
, so that you can reduce the time as much as possible. Let's use Python-style pseudocode to describe the program (although in practice it is most common to use languages like, C, C++, and Rust where optimal program latencies are required):
â
def
on_market_trade
(
self, instrument, market_trade
):
model_value = self.compute_model_value(instrument, market_trade)
order = self.compute_order_decision(instrument, model_value)
if
order
is
not
None
:
self.send_order(order)
A reasonable place to start in understanding the latency of your critical codepath is to wrap timers around the functions doing the heavy lifting:
def
on_market_trade
(
self, instrument, market_trade
):
start_time = datetime.now()
model_value = self.compute_model_value(instrument, market_trade)
order = self.compute_order_decision(instrument, model_value)
end_time = datetime.now()
self.add_time_sample(end_time - start_time)
if
order
is
not
None
:
self.send_order(order)
The function
self.add_time_sample
would add the elapsed time to a histogram that you could print statistics for at the end of your programâs lifecycle, or on some regular basis based on time or number of samples observed.
There are many issues with the above approach:
It measures the time required to compute the order decision, but does not include the time it takes to send the actual order.
It observes computation time on every market trade, rather than just the trades that result in orders â this can bias results because the most interesting times to send orders may be the ones where your program is running the slowest due to volume of market events or other factors.
datetime.now()
itself is a slow, expensive function that can impact the runtime speed and memory profile of the code above, which adds up if your program is already operating on a microsecond-timescale. The typical way to fix this last issue is to use native performance counters that most programming language have primitives to access.
Hereâs a new code sample that attempts to fix the above:
def
on_market_trade
(
self, instrument, market_trade
):
start_time = time.perf_counter_ns()
model_value = self.compute_model_value(instrument, market_trade)
order = self.compute_order_decision(instrument, model_value)
if
order
is
not
None
:
self.send_order(order)
end_time = time.perf_counter_ns()
self.add_time_sample(end_time - start_time)
This is an improvement, but are we really getting at the full latency of the trading system? The above doesnât include significant elements of the critical path, including the time to parse the market trade update, or anything involving network I/O. Letâs take a step back and trace a market data update through the complete critical path of the
automated trading system (ATS)
:
Network packet containing the market trade hits the network card of the box where the ATS is running (sent from the exchange)
The packet is passed to the runtime of the ATS
The ATS parses the bytes of the packet to pull out necessary fields (such as trade price or trade size)
The ATS computes a model value and makes a decision to send an order
The internal memory representation of the order is converted to the protocol of the exchange that the order is being sent to
The ATS makes function calls to

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于使用半潜船进行走私活动的技术选择和有效性讨论

不同观点：
• [hugoromano] 认为选择天线不当，建议使用Starlink Mini以避免因振荡和盐暴露导致的电机损坏。同时质疑实时通信的必要性，提出"发射后不管"的策略即可。
• [greenavocado] 预测未来将有大量由卡特尔铺设的纤维光缆从哥伦比亚延伸到美国。
• [willvarfar] 提到H I Sutton是相关领域的权威，主流媒体常跟随其研究和视频获取信息。
• [rkagerer] 质疑为何不跟踪船只以逮捕接头人，并指出在哥伦比亚操作半潜船是非法的。
• [bob1029] 对作为卡特尔开发人员或系统工程师的体验感到好奇。
• [julianeon] 提到目前毒品活动的中心已转移到墨西哥，哥伦比亚的影响力下降。
• [Roark66] 开玩笑说下一艘船会自己铺设300公里的纤维光缆。
• [stickfigure] 主张合法化以解决此类问题。
• [tczMUFlmoNk] 对Starlink天线在水下的工作效果感到好奇，或者船只需要浮出水面进行通信。

• 对未来技术发展的猜测和调侃：如自铺设纤维光缆和无人机运送技术的应用。

data.title: Volunteer finds Holy Grail of abolitionist-era Baptist documents
data.author: ohjeez
data.article_summary: 历史学家詹妮弗·克罗马克在马萨诸塞州格罗顿的美国浸礼会档案馆发现了一份有178年历史的反奴隶制卷轴，题为《反对奴隶制的决议和抗议》，签署于1847年3月2日，由116名新英格兰牧师签署。这份文件在2025年5月被发现前，曾一度被认为已经遗失。该文件揭示了18世纪美国东北部关于奴隶制的争论，并突显了浸礼会历史上的关键时刻——1845年南方浸礼会因奴隶制问题与北方分裂，成立了南方浸礼会。文件表达了对奴隶制的反对，并呼吁正义，在南北战争前夕具有重要历史意义。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于历史文件的发现及其保存状态的讨论

不同观点：
• [kashunstva] 引用的 [thaumasiotes] 指出，该文件在被发现之前已经有复印件存在，这次发现的是原件，内容是116位浸信会牧师反对美国奴隶制的公开信。这表明美国浸信会曾努力在各大学图书馆寻找此文件，最终发现它被保存在自己的档案中。

• [Apocryphon] 认为，许多档案和收藏可能尚未对其所有物品进行扫描和数字化保存。同时，对近年来在一些被毁图书馆中永远丢失的作品表示遗憾，并引用了维基百科上关于被毁图书馆的条目来支持其观点。

补充讨论：
• 文件的发现过程和其历史意义成为讨论的一个重点，尤其是它对反对奴隶制的历史见证作用。
• 数字化保存的必要性和紧迫性被提出，尤其是考虑到历史上许多重要文献因各种原因被毁或丢失。

Historian Jennifer Cromack points out the word “Slavery” on a recently found, 178-year-old anti-slavery scroll at Grotonwood, the home mission of The American Baptist Churches of Massachusetts, Thursday, June 26, 2025, in Groton, Mass. (AP Photo/Charles Krupa)
By
Associated Press
UPDATED:
July 3, 2025 at 11:43 AM EDT
By MICHAEL CASEY
GROTON, Mass. (AP) — Jennifer Cromack was combing through the American Baptist archive when she uncovered a slim box among some 18th and 19th century journals. Opening it, she found a scroll in pristine condition.
A closer look revealed the 5-foot-long (1.5-meter-long) document was a handwritten declaration titled “A Resolution and Protest Against Slavery,” signed by 116 New England ministers in
Boston
and adopted March 2, 1847. Until its discovery in May at the archives in Groton, Massachusetts, American Baptist officials worried the
anti-slavery document
had been lost forever after fruitless searches at Harvard and
Brown universities
and other locations. A copy was last seen in a 1902 history book.
“I was just amazed and excited,” Cromack, a retired teacher who volunteers at the archive, said. “We made a find that really says something to the people of the state and the people in the country. … It speaks of their commitment to keeping people safe and out of situations that they should not be in.”
The document offers a glimpse into an emerging debate over slavery in the 18th century in the Northeast. The document was signed 14 years before the start of the Civil War as a growing number of religious leaders were starting to speak out against slavery.
Historian Jennifer Cromack holds a recently found, 178-year-old anti-slavery scroll at Grotonwood, the home mission of The American Baptist Churches of Massachusetts, Thursday, June 26, 2025, in Groton, Mass. (AP Photo/Charles Krupa)
Historian Jennifer Cromack, left, and Rev. Diane Badger unfurl a recently found, 178-year-old anti-slavery scroll which was found in a storage box at Grotonwood, the home mission of The American Baptist Churches of Massachusetts, Thursday, June 26, 2025, in Groton, Mass. (AP Photo/Charles Krupa)
Rev. Diane Badger unfurls a recently found, 178-year-old anti-slavery scroll at Grotonwood, the home mission of The American Baptist Churches of Massachusetts, Thursday, June 26, 2025, in Groton, Mass. (AP Photo/Charles Krupa)

Split over slavery
The document also shines a spotlight on a critical moment in the history of
the Baptist church
.
It was signed two years after the issue of slavery prompted southern Baptists to split from northern Baptists and form the
Southern Baptist Convention,
the nation’s largest Protestant denomination. The split in 1845 followed a ruling by the American Baptist Foreign Mission Society prohibiting slave owners from becoming missionaries. The northern Baptists eventually became American Baptist Churches USA.
“It comes from such a critical era in American history, you know, right prior to the Civil War,” said the Rev. Mary Day Hamel, the executive minister of the American Baptist Churches of Massachusetts.
“It was a unique moment in history when Baptists in Massachusetts stepped up and took a strong position and stood for justice in the shaping of this country,” she said. “That’s become part of our heritage to this day, to be people who stand for justice, for American Baptists to embrace diversity.”
A risky declaration
Deborah Bingham Van Broekhoven, the executive director emerita of the American Baptist Historical Society, said many Americans at the time, especially in the North, were “undecided” about slavery and weren’t sure how to respond or were worried about speaking out.
“They thought it was a southern problem, and they had no business getting involved in what they saw as the state’s rights,” Van Broekhoven said. “Most Baptists, prior to this, would have refrained from this kind of protest. This is a very good example of them going out on a limb and trying to be diplomatic.”

44477235.article_summary: 历史学家詹妮弗·克罗马克在马萨诸塞州格罗顿的美国浸礼会档案馆发现了一份有178年历史的反奴隶制卷轴，题为《反对奴隶制的决议和抗议》，签署于1847年3月2日，由116名新英格兰牧师签署。这份文件在2025年5月被发现前，曾一度被认为已经遗失。该文件揭示了18世纪美国东北部关于奴隶制的争论，并突显了浸礼会历史上的关键时刻——1845年南方浸礼会因奴隶制问题与北方分裂，成立了南方浸礼会。文件表达了对奴隶制的反对，并呼吁正义，在南北战争前夕具有重要历史意义。

• ClojureScript在生产环境中的调试复杂性（tekacs提出的观点），以及在实际应用中保留足够信息以便调试的难度。

data.title: Hugging Your Cactus
data.author: ozgrakkurt
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了“拥抱仙人掌”这一比喻，源自罗伯特·唐尼在颁奖礼上介绍梅尔·吉布森时的演讲。唐尼谈到了吉布森在他困境时给予的支持和建议：不要放弃希望，找到基于宽恕的信仰，并勇于承担错误责任，拥抱自己的丑陋面（即“拥抱仙人掌”），从中学会谦卑，让生活获得新意义。文章进一步阐述了这一过程包括从羞耻、破碎到谦卑、治愈的旅程，强调不要孤立自己，要在群体中找到希望和支持。关键在于接受宽恕，既要原谅他人，也要原谅自己，从而实现真正的个人转变。拥抱仙人掌的过程虽痛苦，但通过面对和处理这些痛苦，可以获得真实的希望和人生的新意义。

The metaphor of “hugging the cactus” originates from a speech that the actor Robert Downey gave as he was introducing his friend Mel Gibson during an award presentation.  During this time Gibson was going through some public struggles of his own and was a somewhat unexpected choice for the honor.  “To some surprise, Downey gave the gift of public acceptance to the embattled actor [Gibson]; …the defense was a return of kindness for Downey.  Gibson gave “The Avengers” actor a job in 2003’s “The Singing Detective” after his drug arrests made him uninsurable.”
[1]
With this time in mind, Downey reflected on the following advice his friend had once offered him:
Here is a link to the speech itself:
“Actually I asked Mel to present me with this reward for a reason.  When I couldn’t get sober, he told me not to give up hope, and he urged me to find my faith. It didn’t have to be his faith or anyone else’s, as long as it was rooted in forgiveness. And I couldn’t get hired, so he cast me as the lead in a movie that was actually developed for him. He kept a roof over my head, and he kept food on the table. And most importantly, he said if I accepted responsibility for my wrongdoings and if I embraced that part of my soul that was ugly — “hugging the cactus” he calls it — he said that if I “hugged the cactus” long enough, I’d become a man of some humility and that my life would take on a new meaning. And I did, and it worked. All he asked in return was that someday I help the next guy in some small way. It’s reasonable to assume that at the time he didn’t imagine that the next guy would be him or that someday was tonight.”
[2]
In this short yet powerful speech, several concepts form around this idea of hugging your cactus.  Looking at it more closely one can see the outline of a cactus hugging journey being mapped out; a journey from shame, brokenness and false or shadow self toward humility, healing, a more holistic sense of self, and ultimately a life of new meaning.  This is an invitation to deny or “die to” self or ego and is laid out in six parts that are best seen more fluidly than as rigid sequential steps.  The following brief unpacking and application of this speech has been influenced from research toward my Doctor of Ministry thesis project at Gordon-Conwell Theological Seminary.
When life is not working don’t give up hope
Life, or at least a part of life not working means that something has gone wrong, perhaps even for an extended period of time.  The 12 Step tradition refers to this as “life as no longer manageable.”  One important point here is that in hugging your cactus a self-inflicted crisis is directly related to one’s life not working.  This could be a single really bad choice, a pattern of behavior, or something in between.  Whatever the reason when one realizes this, it is important not to lose or give up their hope that things can get better, that healing and an authentic personal transformation is possible.  This healing happens best in community, so here it is important for one not to isolate their self in despair, but instead find others who can be a source of hope, support, and encouragement.  It is also important here to recognize that the sense of despair and hopelessness is there for a reason. Therefore it’s also important to not move on from hopelessness too soon.  Instead, lean into it and learn from it, for the cactus hugging journey does involve dealing with pain, even self inflicted pain.  Working through despair can actually be an important part of connecting with authentic hope; however, it is also important not to stay in hopelessness too long as hope is an essential part of the cactus hugging journey.
Find a faith rooted in forgiveness
Closely related to the idea of hope in the cactus hugging journey is faith, specifically a faith that is rooted in forgiveness.  The alternative here is a faith rooted in performance or perfection, and yet, simply trying harder does not work.  Forgiveness is key in accepting that one is responsible for the crisis that has led to their life not working, and forgiveness takes practice; without forgiveness there can be no real or lasting hope.  It is also worth noting that the ability to both give and receive forgiveness are equally important here and that often the most difficult person to forgive is one’s self.
Take personal responsibility for wrongdoings
It is worth noting that accepting and taking responsibility for wrong doings is very difficult, yet this is also where real change can start to happen.  Self awareness comes into play in a strong way here as one comes to terms with their real self, the part of self that has caused harm to others.  This again is painful, yet it is why one must lean into the pain and despair, but not stay there either.  This is closely related to forgiveness, for a true sense of forgiveness actually promotes greater p

data.title: A Canadian's AI hoax duped the media and propelled a 'band' to success
data.author: empressplay
data.article_summary: 一名自称为Andrew Frelon的加拿大人通过使用AI工具生成音乐，并假扮成一个名为The Velvet Sundown的乐队发言人，成功欺骗了媒体，使该乐队在Spotify上获得了数百万的月听众。尽管他对此表示道歉，但称这个社会工程实验太具吸引力，无法停止。乐队的音乐出现在多个热门播放列表中，但由于乐队成员没有数字足迹且从未现场演出，引发了质疑。Frelon后来承认整个事件是一个艺术骗局，甚至他在Rolling Stone采访中提供的信息大多是虚假的。这一复杂骗局引发了关于AI使用和文化现象的广泛讨论。

44477151.article_content:
Entertainment
How a Canadian's AI hoax duped the media and propelled a 'band' to streaming success
A Canadian who duped journalists in an elaborate hoax involving Spotify, AI and a suspicious rock band says he apologizes to anyone hurt by his experiment but that it's been "too fascinating" to turn away from.
Pretended to represent The Velvet Sundown as a 'social engineering' experiment
Kevin Maimann
·
CBC News
·
Posted: Jul 05, 2025 9:03 PM EDT | Last Updated: 3 hours ago
The Velvet Sundown uses this image as its profile photo on Spotify and social media. The band's music, which is made with artificial intelligence tools, has become the centre of an elaborate hoax.
(Facebook)
Social Sharing
A Canadian who duped journalists in an elaborate AI music hoax says he apologizes to anyone hurt by his experiment but that it's been "too fascinating" to turn away from.
A man using the pseudonym Andrew Frelon posed as the spokesperson for a band called The Velvet Sundown — which he later said he had no involvement with — creating a media frenzy that propelled the AI-assisted "band" to a million monthly listeners on Spotify.
He spoke with CBC News over the phone Friday on condition that his real name not be revealed. CBC News agreed not to use his real name because he fears harassment based on the hateful messages he's received online, and worries he would lose work if identified.
The sticky online saga began when the band appeared on music streaming platforms several weeks ago and amassed hundreds of thousands of streams from two full-length albums.
Its blend of laid-back 1970s-inspired rock and modern indie pop appeared on several popular Spotify playlists, including one featuring Vietnam War songs.
Commotion
Timbaland used an independent producer's work to train AI — but without the artist's consent
AI song sparks debate in Francophone music scene
But savvy listeners noticed something was off. The band's supposed members had no digital footprint, and there was no record of them ever having performed live. The album art and profile photo, featuring four shaggy-haired rockers, also carried hallmarks of generative AI.
But as the controversy gained steam, an account on
social media platform X
purporting to represent the band emphatically denied that any of the music was created by artificial intelligence, calling the accusations "lazy" and "baseless."
CBC reached out to the X account on Wednesday and attempted to arrange an interview through a Gmail account purporting to represent the band.
Then, a man calling himself Andrew Frelon
told Rolling Stone
, in an article that was published online later that day, that he is behind The Velvet Sundown and the X account, and that he used generative AI platform Suno to create the songs. He called the project an "art hoax."
WATCH | Expert speaks on AI regulation:
Why more needs to be done to regulate the use of AI
1 year ago
Duration
6:07
New research out of Western University is shining a light on the federal government's use of artificial intelligence through a Tracking Automated Government Register. Joanna Redden, an associate professor of Information and Media Studies and co-director at Starling: Just Technologies. Just Societies. and Data Justice Lab, joined London Morning to talk about the data and concerns about AI use.
But just as the mystery appeared to be solved, a different X account linked to the official Velvet Sundown Spotify page
posted a statement
saying Frelon has nothing to do with the band.
"Someone is attempting to hijack the identity of The Velvet Sundown," said the statement, which also appeared on the band's Spotify and Instagram accounts on Thursday.
That same day, Frelon, who gave the Rolling Stone interview,
posted a lengthy blog
confirming he had nothing to do with the band and that nearly everything he told the magazine, including his name, was a lie.
The actual band's identity was once again a mystery. It turned out the hoax was, in fact, part of a bigger hoax.
'It's too fascinating of a mystery'
Speaking with CBC News on Friday, Frelon maintained that he has "zero" connection to the Velvet Sundown.
Asked about his motivation for maintaining such a complicated ruse, Frelon said the way the whole thing has played out has become like "artistic jet fuel."
"There's so many weird cultural, technical things at play here. It's too fascinating of a mystery for me to turn away from," he said.
The real person behind Andrew Frelon is an expert on web platform safety and policy issues, with extensive experience using generative AI. He was born in the United States but lives in Canada.
A man calling himself Andrew Frelon says he used AI to generate this image of The Velvet Sundown.
(Andrew Frelon)
Several major American publications have interviewed him about his other AI projects and safety and policy issues work.
CBC News verified his identity through screen shots and a Signal video chat. Frelon sent screen shots of his correspondence with Rolling Stone to confirm

data.title: Ask HN: Advice for Starting a Hacker Space?
data.author: pkdpic
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：创办和运营一个成功的 makerspace/hackerspace 所涉及的各个方面，包括组织、管理、财务、社区建设和潜在问题。

不同观点：
• dv35z 认为该书是创办 makerspace/hackerspace 的“黄金标准”，涵盖了工具组织、人员配置、标准操作程序、敏捷方法、创业、资金等多方面内容，并提供了书籍链接。
• bsenftner 根据创办和运营 Droplabs 的经验，强调需要将所有正式成员及其行为和财务义务书面化，包括惩罚措施，以应对不遵守规定的情况。此外，还需要明确组织决策过程以防止无休止的讨论。
• jerkstate 指出商业性质的 hackerspace 面临更多问题，建议专注于社区规模的小型 hackerspace，并提出了一系列实际操作建议，如责任豁免、项目设计和志愿者机会。
• mjsir911 强调“Just do it”的态度，建议先找到物理空间并开始聚会，通过口碑吸引合适的社区成员，同时分享了欧洲风格 hackerspace 的经验，并提到创办过程中的试错和乐趣。
• Tomte 提供了一个设计模式的链接，并提到“Tuesday Rule”作为一个有用的规则。
• CursedSilicon 提到了西雅图地区的两个 hackerspace，并强调维持积极氛围和将空间打造成“第三空间”的重要性。
• yummypaint 建议从电子废物回收商或垃圾填埋场获取免费或廉价的物品供孩子们拆解和再利用。
• threatofrain 认为如果只是一个车库里的计算机俱乐部，不需要太多规划，因为空间和组织复杂性有限。
• kulahan 建议与当地图书馆合作，捐赠主要工具以获取支持。
• mandeepj 指出需要大量资金购买设备，除非专注于非常具体的利基市场。
• MongooseStudios 表示对该想法的支持，没有具体建议。
• cranberryturkey 开玩笑说如果有资金，会买一个便宜的房子改造成 hackerspace。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了多个实际操作中的具体问题，如财务管理、成员行为规范、项目设计、社区合作和空间利用等。
• 争议的焦点在于商业性质和社区规模的 hackerspace 之间的差异，以及如何有效管理和维持一个积极的社区氛围。
• 不同建议提供了多种视角，从实际经验分享到具体操作指南，涵盖了创办和运营 hackerspace 的多个方面。

data.title: Tesla opens 168 stall Supercharger station, with solar farm and big batteries
data.author: decimalenough
data.article_summary: Tesla在加州Lost Hills开设了一个大型超级充电站，占地30英亩，目前有84个充电桩投入使用，最终将扩展至168个，成为世界上最大的充电站。该站点配备11兆瓦的太阳能阵列，包括太阳能遮阳棚和邻近的太阳能农场，以及10个Tesla Megapack电池，完全由太阳能供电并可离网运行。每个V4超级充电桩功率为325千瓦，其中12个为可直接通过的设计，方便拖挂车或船只的电动车主充电。该站点位于I-5州际公路旁，是全球最繁忙的电动车走廊之一，预计剩余的充电桩和休息区将在今年圣诞节前开放。充电费用为每千瓦时0.62美元，对所有使用北美充电标准（NACS）插头的电动车开放。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：充电站的布局及收费标准是否合理

不同观点：
• Rebelgecko认为充电站布局稀疏但每个站点有更多充电桩是更好的选择。他觉得这种布局虽然有些反直觉，但可能是更优的方案。
• 对于充电费用（60¢+/kWh），Rebelgecko表达了对回本时间的担忧，暗示当前的收费标准可能偏高，导致回本周期较长。

补充讨论：
• 关于充电站布局的讨论中，存在不同偏好。有人可能认为密集的充电站布局更方便用户使用，而另一些人如Rebelgecko则倾向于更广分布但每个站点拥有更多充电桩的布局。
• 收费标准问题引发了对经济性的关注，60¢+/kWh的收费水平是否合理，取决于充电需求和竞争对手的定价，同时也关系到充电站的运营成本和回本速度。
• 争议焦点在于充电站的布局和收费标准的平衡：如何在用户便利性和经济效益之间找到最佳的解决方案。
